articleTitle: Secure & Traceable Companies File Management System Using Blockchain and IPFS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: With the advancement of cloud-based file management platforms, sharing and storing files in the company's area can be easily achieved through a variety of file-sharing platforms. However, these platforms often lack of security and adequate access logs or activity records for the shared files, resulting in a lack of control and traceability for users. This research proposes an traceable and secure system for managing files in companies using blockchain and IPFS. The content ID of uploaded files to IPFS will be stored on the blockchain along with user access rights and access logs. Integration with the existing company file management system is also facilitated by the use of the change data capture method. Experimental findings demonstrate that the system offers the desired traceability of access and activity while also meeting data security requirements such as confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Furthermore, performance tests indicate satisfactory outcomes with 0.8 seconds per MB for file storage on IPFS, and 4.1 seconds per transaction for data storage on Blockchain. The experimental results revealed that the proposed system, integrating blockchain and IPFS, successfully addressed the need for traceability of access and activity for the company's data, providing a significant improvement in data security and management over existing solutions.

articleTitle: Wireless Edge Controller for Robot Education Using MQTT on Dobot Magician Lite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The integration of wireless controllers in robot education has emerged as a pivotal area to enhance the learning experience and practical understanding of robotics concepts. This paper presents the implementation of a wireless controller for educational purposes using MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) on the Dobot Magician Lite robotic platform. MQTT, a lightweight messaging protocol, facilitates efficient communication between the controller and the robot, enabling seamless interaction and control over the robot's movements and functionalities. The implementation focuses on providing a user-friendly interface and intuitive controls, allowing students and educators to easily operate the robot while exploring various educational scenarios. Leveraging MQTT's flexibility, the system offers real-time control and monitoring capabilities, fostering interactive learning experiences in robotics education. The proposed wireless controller demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of employing MQTT in robot education, paving the way for enhanced learning opportunities and practical applications in the field of robotics. The examination of MQTT performance across various bandwidths provides important insights into our system's abilities. At 8 Mbps, our system achieved its highest transaction speed, averaging 1.61 transactions per second with a quick average transaction time of 0.62 seconds. Transaction speeds decreased as bandwidth decreased, with 1 Mbps showing the slowest average TPS of 1.24. Importantly, data retention stayed at 100% for all bandwidths, demonstrating consistent reliability.

articleTitle: SecureGuard: An IoT-Based Home Security Solution for High-Burglary Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: SecureGuard presents an intelligent IoT based home security solution tailored to combat rising burglary rates in hotspot areas. This paper details the development of an innovative home security website that integrates facial recognition, PIN code verification, and machine learning algorithms. Through a structured methodology, the solution offers robust authentication and predictive analysis capabilities, significantly enhancing home protection. We have presented a detailed design and development of Secure-Guard using a 3-layered IoT solution architecture. Our prototype demonstrates the potential of this solution in securing homes and contributing to smart city development, promoting sustainability. Additionally, we summarized a list of issues related to this smart home security solution, including social, economic, and ethical considerations.

articleTitle: DRAKE's as a Smart Solution for Surveying, Mapping, and Modeling Based on Artificial Intelligence to Determine the Feasibility of the Land
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Plantation is a sector that plays a very large role in developing the economy in Indonesia, especially oil palm plantations. Oil palm is one of the plantation crops that is in great demand by entrepreneurs in Indonesia. Apart from that, palm oil has become one of the main commodities produced by Indonesian plantations which has been exported to several countries. Based on the final report by the Indonesian Ministry of Trade in 2015, it was stated that in the future the amount of world consumption of palm oil will be higher than the amount of production. Looking at the problem, the proposer found a solution that could help palm oil business players map land locations. The proposer offers a solution to this problem, namely by using drone tracking DRAKE's (Drone Kece Unesa) is a smart solution based on drone technology that can be used to survey, map, and model coconut plantation land by utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. This tool is equipped with AI technology which can process data collected by drones in a short time and produce accurate and detailed results about the condition of coconut plantation land. AI technology also allows this tool to recognize and map coconut plants and analyze the suitability of land for coconut plantations. By using this technology, farmers or coconut plantation investors can obtain accurate and detailed information about the condition of the land to be planted with coconuts and analyze the suitability of the land for coconut plantations more easily and quickly. This can help them make the right decisions in developing coconut plantations and increase the productivity and efficiency of coconut plantation businesses. With this tool, the process of surveying and mapping coconut plantation land can be carried out more efficiently, quickly, and accurately than traditional methods. This technology can also help oil palm farmers make better decisions regarding plantation location selection, crop planning, and overall land management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Musical Immersion: A Multimodal Framework Integrating GSR Signals with Visual Art Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study delves into the application of integrated technologies for music visualization, aiming to convey the emotional state of DJs during performances through visual expression, thereby enriching the visual dimension of their shows. The system architecture incorporates three distinct technologies: Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) sensors to detect the DJ's emotional state, Touch Designer to amalgamate visual elements, and Stable Diffusion for image generation.

articleTitle: Balinese Dance Attributes Utilizing Augmented Reality with Marker Based Tracking Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)

authors.preferredName: Ni Luh Komang Ratna Indraswari D.

abstract: This study presents the design, implementation, and testing of an application for introducing Balinese dance attributes using Augmented Reality (AR) with a Marker Based Tracking method. The application aims to enhance user knowledge about the meanings and attributes of Balinese dances, specifically Tari Pendet, Tari Legong, and Tari Tedung Sari. The research began with data collection, system analysis, system design, creation of 3D objects, user interface implementation, and blackbox testing. The marker-based tracking method allows users to view 3D objects by scanning markers provided within the application. The blackbox testing results confirmed that the application functions as expected. Furthermore, user experience and satisfaction were evaluated using a User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) with 35 respondents. The UEQ results indicated positive evaluations, with scores of 1.890 for Attractiveness, 1.380 for Perspicuity, 1.450 for Efficiency, 1.735 for Dependability, 1.535 for Stimulation, and 1.440 for Novelty. These findings demonstrate that the application is effective in providing cultural education and promoting the preservation of Balinese dance traditions through interactive and engaging technology.

articleTitle: Ontology-Driven Semantic Models for Balinese Lontar Manuscript Knowledge Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The Balinese Lontar manuscripts hold significant historical and cultural value, encapsulating intricate knowledge and traditions. This research explores the application of ontology-driven semantic models as a method for knowledge representation of these manuscripts. Utilizing Semantic technologies, the study aims to develop explicit representation formats that capture the detailed knowledge embedded within the manuscripts. Ontologies are employed to structure and organize this information, enabling systematic categorization and tailored presentations based on user preferences. The research highlights the growth of ontology-driven approaches in various domains, demonstrating their utility in formalizing knowledge representations and enhancing the understanding of complex information. In the context of Balinese Lontar manuscripts, ontology technology streamlines the categorization and annotation processes, facilitating the creation of comprehensive datasets for further analysis. The intersection of ontology-driven semantic models with cultural heritage preservation presents a unique opportunity to safeguard and promote traditional knowledge systems. By developing an ontology tailored to the nuances of Balinese culture, this study provides a robust framework for preserving and disseminating the unique cultural heritage contained within Lontar manuscripts. This research contributes to the body of knowledge at the intersection of ontology, cultural heritage, and information technology, offering insights into the challenges, methodologies, and implications of such an approach.

articleTitle: Impact of Inter-Screen Distance on Visual Clarity in Fixed-Optical System HMD Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Inter-pupillary distance (IPD), the distance between the pupils of the eyes, varies among individuals and is a crucial human factor in ensuring clear image perception in head-mounted display environments. Although adjusting the lens distance within the device to match the IPD would be ideal, it is impractical due to cost and design constraints. Therefore, our study proposed to adjust the inter-screen distance (ISD) instead, and investigated the conditions for clear image. Our results revealed there exists conditions of ISD that forms a clear image, However, the range is not dependent IPD and varies among individuals, potentially influenced by the user's ocular movements. Additionally, we found that the ISD range for clear image becomes narrower for smaller objects. These findings suggest the importance of providing customized ISD conditions for each user to ensure optimal image.

articleTitle: Fronthaul Design and Analysis with Radio over Fiber and Wavelength Division Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Radio over Fiber (RoF) emerges as a promising candidate for 5G networks, particularly in cloud radio access network (CRAN) systems, where centralized signal processing offers reduced latency and enhanced transfer speeds. Millimeter Waves (mmWave) are gaining attention for their potential in high-capacity, long-range communication systems, further fueling the 5G revolution. This research proposes a design employing a 4×1 RoF scheme using Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) with Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) as a dispersion compensator. Simulation results demonstrate the viability of both downstream and upstream configurations, meeting International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Standards for Q Factor and Bit Error Rate (BER). While challenges such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) decline with transmission distance persists, strategic system design and component selection is essential for mitigating these issues, ensuring optimal performance in 5G networks.

articleTitle: Crafting AI-Driven Open Educational Resources (OER) Videos for Enhanced German Language Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop Open Educational Resources (OER) video materials with the assistance of AI applications. The product development follows a seven-step video development design model, which includes (1) creating a narrative script with the help of ChatGPT 4.0, (2) generating voice-over from the composed narration, (3) producing image generated content from the script using leonardo-ai, (4) creating animation from the generated images through runaway-ai, (5) combining voice-over with the generated video, (6) merging multiple videos into a single video, and (7) revising the product. While images generated by leonardo-ai can be diverse, they often do not align with the requested prompt. The researcher had to revise the prompt several times to obtain images that met the researcher's preferences. Similarly, in the context of generating videos through AI, the researcher had to undergo multiple iterations to find the desired video animation. Thus, it can be concluded that crafting an appropriate prompt is crucial in generating images and videos.

articleTitle: Blood Vessel Segmentation on MRA (Magnetic Resonance Angiography) Using U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Blood vessels are a vital component of the cardiovas-cular system which supports the life and health of the entire body, including the brain. Disrupted blood vessels can have a serious impact on health and quality of life. The important functions of blood vessels include distributing oxygen and nutrients, removing waste, regulating body temperature, transporting hormones, the immune system and helping the wound healing process. Blood vessels in the brain can be used to diagnose cardiovascular and neurological diseases including stroke, aneurysm, epilepsy, migraine, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, neuritis etc. U-Net is a convolutional neural network architecture that works well in image segmentation with limited datasets with fairly good accuracy results. The process stages carried out include pre-processing MRA (Magnetic Resonance Angiography) data, U-Net model training and performance evaluation. The expected results are able to detect blood vessels in the brain from MRA data with a high level of accuracy so that it can contribute as a tool in clinical diagnosis that is useful in the medical field. U-Net is able to segment blood vessels on MRA well. From the research results, we got a fairly high level of accuracy and a low level of loss.

articleTitle: A Plastic Waste Hotspot Detection System and Its Application to Measuring Environmental Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper describes a Plastic Waste Hotspot Detection System which has been developed in an international collaborative research project to realize an “Environmental AI-Human Actions integration” with marine plastic waste reduction actions. In this project, various local conditions are obtained to the system to realize an environmentally resilient society. The nature conservation activities such as marine plastic waste collection and reduction actions are implemented based on these conditions. In the process of integration of Environmental AI and Human Actions, the effects of these activities and activists' contribution to environmental improvement and global-scale knowledge are accumulated, shared, analyzed, and visualized through global-scale analysis. This paper describes the Plastic Waste Hotspot Detection system as one of the systems that integrate AI systems and human actions. This paper examines the feasibility and effectiveness of the system through the fieldwork tests in Phuket, Thailand and Surabaya, Indonesia.

articleTitle: Correlation Study: Emotion Recognition and Verbal Skills in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Children with ASD struggle to recognize other people's emotional expressions. They are rooted in the cognitive process's weakness in understanding others' feelings and impacting the ability to establish relationships. This study explores the relationship between the ability to recognize basic expressions with verbal skills, the ability to understand simple commands, and social motivation. The method used in this study is quantitative. The descriptive study was conducted to describe the response of 15 students with ASD. The data analysis technique uses Kendall's Tau. A total of 8 subjects or 53.3 %, couldn't recognize emotional expressions, 28.7% could recognize emotional expressions, and 20% could somewhat recognize emotional expressions. The total, 40% can answer simple questions and express their wishes verbally. A total of 33.3 % experienced echolalia. While 26.7% are nonverbal, they cannot speak or have limited speaking skills. There is a significant relationship between emotional recognition skills with an understanding of simple commands and social motivation, and there is a relationship between speaking skills or oral skills with an understanding of simple commands and social motivation.

articleTitle: Improving Biometric Accuracy Using Ear Canal Images: Removing Overexposed and Underexposed Images Through a Lightweight Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Extensive research has been conducted on high-security personal authentication using DNNs, such as facial, fingerprint, and voice recognition. However, these biometric methods have accuracy issues under certain conditions, such as in dark environments like night-time, when gloves or masks are worn or in the presence of background noise. To address these challenges, our study focuses on the use of images of the ear canal which is a highly individual characteristic that can be easily captured and is unaffected by the environment. Previous research involved manually removing noisy images, such as those overexposed or underexposed, before conducting accuracy evaluations, achieving an F1-Score of 1.0 with clean data. Additionally, systems that utilize DNNs suffer from high power consumption due to GPU usage and expensive computational resources. In our research, we aim to enhance accuracy through an automated detection of overexposed and underexposed images using a simple algorithm. We also opted for the EfficientNet model which is high computational efficiency. Our results showed an improvement in the F1-Score to 0.99968, an increase of 0.0019 compared to before noise removal. Furthermore, by conducting a five-fold cross-validation not previously performed, we demonstrated no decrease in accuracy, thus indicating the versatility of using ear canal images for personal authentication. The misclassified images we analyzed included significant blurring near walls, faintly shadowed images, and blurred images. Future work will explore methods to resolve these issues and examine more lightweight models suitable for operation on edge devices.

articleTitle: On the Spatial Point Pattern on Customer Affect Retail Fuel Stations Businesses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Retail fuel stations need to plan business development to increase profitability despite high market competition. The patterns of people's habits and fuel supply dynamics have caused income differences in various fuel retail stations. It is difficult for retail fuel stations to increase the sales of fuel oil because of its reliability. This study aims to investigate the pattern of influence of the distribution of consumer locations on the existence of fuel stations, with the expectation used to maximize land productivity at fuel stations. The main contribution of this research is the modeling of spatial point pattern in examining factors affecting customer demography of the facility variability in the closest fuel stations for each district. This can be obtained by applying the stochastics processes couple with Generalized Linear Models (GLMs), namely the regression modeling to the non-homogenous Poisson Process (NHPP) data as the observation related to the customer location and competence of the fuel stations as the counting data. Two modeling structure scenarios were performed based on the type of the response data around 18 district, i.e. homogenous and non-homogenous Poisson model. The best model is chosen by selecting the smallest Akaike Information Criteria (AIC) value. It is found that the non-homogenous model is superior model with the leading AIC at 95% better than the one level model. We found that, in the long term, customer visit intensity has significant impact to number of pump capacity and merchant store. Future research should explore the other covariate and customer choice strategy when refuelling.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Helical Antenna for Wireless Communications Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The axial mode helical antennas have a compact design and directional radiation mode, particularly for handheld wireless communications systems. However, the axial mode helix antenna has the disadvantages of large size and narrow bandwidth. In this paper, a design of end-fire wideband helical antenna with a parasitic circular patch is proposed. The antenna structure consists of 4 turns and FR-4 ground plane. A copper plate parasitic circular patch placed over the driven helix. Directivity, VSWR, bandwidth, reflection coefficient, and radiation pattern of the proposed antenna are studied. Measured results shows that the proposed antenna has an ultra-wide impedance bandwidth (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ -10dB) which covers from 2133.1 MHZ to 2754.7 MHz. The reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ -10dB) resulting value of -52.80 dB at the center frequency and VSWR of 1.02. Moreover, maximum directivity of antenna achieved peak gain of 9.48 dBi. The proposed design achieved a simple structure, ultra-wide bandwidth, and can be used for 2.4 GHz wideband Wi-Fi applications.

articleTitle: Balinese Temple: The Image and Characteristics of Tourists based on Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Bali, as an island, has the most market share of tourism in Indonesia, which gives Bali the potential to become a foreign exchange earner for the country. The progress of tourism has an impact on the economic growth of the community. Temples are the second most popular group of tourist attraction in Bali tourism, so it is important to understand the image of temples and the characteristics of tourists who visit. This research aims to carry out sentiment analysis on reviews of tourists who visit the temple and analyze the results to gain further insight. Based on the proportion of positive reviews versus negative reviews, the Balinese temple generally can be said to have a positive image among tourists. A positive image is related to the perception that the temple is a beautiful and worthwhile place to visit. Meanwhile, the negative image is related to entrance ticket fees, prohibitions on entering temples, additional fees for sarong rentals and local tour guides, as well as parking facilities and the presence of hawker. This research also clustered tourists and produced four groups of tourist characteristics, namely compound tourists with positive reviews, compound tourists with negative reviews, October tourists and September tourists.

articleTitle: Bagging System Performance Analysis Using Artificial Neural Network, Random Forest Regression, Linear Regression, and Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the most important sectors in the world because it provides commodities such as rice, cassava, corn, rubber, and palm oil. Urea fertilizer is essential for use in crops, and the demand for this product increases every year due to rapid globalization. Fertilizer firms must reduce production costs and product losses to remain competitive. This study introduces the use of machine learning to predict which algorithm could give the best result in predicting fertilizer weight losses. The algorithms studied were linear regression, artificial neural network, random forest regression, and support vector regression. The results show R2, MAE, and RMSE for each method. The R2 values for ANN, Random Forest, Linear Regression, and Support Vector Regression are 0.9509; 0.9759; 0.9507; and 0.9367, respectively. Random Forest shows the best result compared with the three other algorithms, implying that it is the most accurate algorithm for this research, followed by the supporting result MAE value of 0.0829, which is smaller than the other.

articleTitle: Balinese Script Handwriting Recognition Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Handwritten Balinese script consists of letters that have unique and complex shapes and adapt to the writer's handwriting. The main challenge in recognizing these characters is the variation in letter shapes due to different writing styles, lighting conditions and varying image quality. The aim of this research is to develop a deep learning model using CNN to recognize handwritten Balinese script. This research has carried out several CNN model configurations with different learning rates. The research results show that the model developed can produce excellent performance with an accuracy rate of 94.4%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Optical Character Recognition Accuracy in Livestock Weighting Systems Through Distributed Intelligent Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This research develops and optimizes an optical character recognition (OCR) system for goat weighing scales using intelligent computer vision and distributed computing to enhance accuracy and efficiency in real-world operational conditions. Images of the scales are captured and processed to remove noise, then recognized using deep learning algorithms. The implementation of distributed computing frameworks like Apache Hadoop and TensorFlow enables efficient parallel processing. Results show a 20% increase in OCR accuracy and a 30% improvement in processing efficiency compared to conventional systems. This integration provides a scalable and reliable solution for applications in the livestock industry, with potential adaptation for various operational conditions and other livestock types.

articleTitle: Abnormality Detection Method from Heartbeat Sound by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Heart disease is currently the second leading cause of death in Japan, and approximately 80% of patients with heart disease are aged 65 years or older. In addition, in the diagnosis of cardiac disease, highly accurate diagnosis is difficult in depopulated and aging areas due not only to the lack of medical equipment but also to the shortage of medical specialists. Therefore, the ultimate goal of this study is to create a system that can automatically diagnose patients with cardiac disease using machine learning from heartbeat sound data transmitted by the patient. As a preliminary step, to investigate effective features for discriminating normal and abnormal heart sounds from heart sounds collected using a digital stethoscope and iStethoscope Pro, and to study the effects of discriminator identification and noise removal on the identification results. The outline of the proposed abnormality detection method is to perform noise processing using spectral gating and a zero-phase filter on the loaded auscultation data. Next, using openSMILE, statistics are calculated from three feature quantities, MFCC (0-14th order), logMelFreqband (0-7th order), and lspFreq (0-7th order), and PCMloudness, which is related to the “volume” of the PCM data. Finally, using WEKA, which is used in machine learning and data mining, a 10-fold cross-validation using SVM and Random Forest (RF) is used to evaluate whether the heart sounds are abnormal or normal. In this study, SVM was shown to be more effective than RF as a discriminative model and spectral gating was more effective than zero-phase filter in noise processing.

articleTitle: A PID Control Algorithm for Path Tracking of a Nonholonomic Car-Like Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: A car-like robot with an Ackermann steering system is a type of nonholonomic which is characterised by a set of first-order differential constraints on its configuration variables, which are not integrable. This distinctive characteristic gives rise to complex issues in the construction of feedback controllers. This research proposes reactive control using a feedback controller using PID algorithm for a car-like robot navigation. The proposed method controls the steering angle of the car-like robot to follow the prescribed path with a constant longitudinal robot velocity. The open-loop car-like dynamical system has been formulated in the form of state-space model. Two PID controllers in parallel computed the lateral position error and the yaw angle error. The summation of the two outputs from the PID controllers was inputted into the state-space model. The PID controller parameters were selected based on trial and error. The simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Securing Smartphone from Mobile Phishing Attacks Using GoogLeNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Nowadays, smartphones have personal and private information about the user; hence, attackers target smartphones to access personal and confidential information. In this context, this paper proposed a googLeNet-based mobile phishing attack detection model. In our propsed model, whenever a user visits a webpage, its screenshot is analyzed by the googLeNet model, and if the website is malicious, the model alerts the user. We used GoogLeNet because it is trained on large amounts of deserts and works efficiently to detect multiclass images. Our model achieves an accuracy of 97.04%, which presents the effectiveness of our proposed model. We also compared the performance of our model with the traditional machine learning model.

articleTitle: Quick Construction Methods of Digital Twins for Outdoor and Indoor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Digital twins can be applied to various practical applications ranging from small-scale indoor models to large-scale outdoor facilities, to enhance and optimize their functionalities using artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) techniques. We present quick construction methods for digital twins applicable to both indoor and outdoor models, and demonstrate how these methods can be implemented using commonly available software packages to evaluate, predict, and enhance the performance of wireless systems.

articleTitle: Determining The Ideal Location For New Branches In Multifinance Companies Using Google Maps API With Clustering Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Selecting the ideal location for new branches is crucial for growth in the multifinance industry, significantly impacting customer interest, sales performance, and profitability. This study employs clustering techniques to analyze large datasets, identify patterns, and predict optimal branch locations based on historical customer data and relevant factors. Utilizing the Google Maps API, the study conducted precise location analysis and visualized customer distribution, including distances between customers and branches. Analyzing personal customer data from 2018–2023 in Bogor and Tangerang, Indonesia, geographic coordinates were obtained for detailed distance and competitor analysis. The Elbow Method identified four optimal clusters using K-medoids clustering, revealing distinct characteristics such as customer location, competition levels, and product preferences. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) visualized these clusters, aiding strategic branch location decisions. This method enhances strategic planning and competitive positioning by accurately identifying market opportunities, enabling multifinance companies to strategically plan branch expansions and drive growth and profitability.

articleTitle: Implementation of Predistortion Technique on OFDM System for LOS and NLOS Environments Using USRP - LabView
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Power Amplifiers (PA) exhibit nonlinear characteristics that can cause nonlinear distortion when applied to OFDM transmission systems, particularly in Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) environments. Nonlinear distortion can adversely affect the performance of modulation schemes in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems, such as signal quality degradation and increased error in symbol detection. This can lead to discrepancies between the transmitted and received data. To address the nonlinear issues of PAs, a predistortion (PD) technique is implemented. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the Saleh model predistortion technique in mitigating nonlinear distortion in OFDM systems. The research is conducted in a real setting using Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) 2920 hardware and LabVIEW software for text data transmission in LOS and NLOS environments. The performance of text data transmission in the OFDM system with applied PD is observed through the constellation diagram and erroneous characters at the receiver. Experimental results demonstrate that the PD technique successfully reduces deviation in symbol constellation points and corrects erroneous characters in both LOS and NLOS environments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Method for Microplastic Identification Using a Combination of Machine Learning and Raman Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Plastic fragments that contain microplastic can have an impact on ecosystems and human health. Since the 1970s, the complexity of microplastic analysis has been a big challenge. This study introduces a machine learning-based approach, which has demonstrated a faster and safer microplastic analysis. In the evaluation, we compare human annotation, machine learning, and image processing methods by using the structural similarity index (SSIM), which shows overall alignment results, except for the Grogol River sample (2). The performance of machine learning is satisfactory, but there are discrepancies in detecting microplastic types in this sample. Notably, the study identifies the potential PP and LDPE microplastics and diverges from human annotation. Our proposed methods are highlighted in the results, which demonstrate 78

articleTitle: PipeBeGood – An AIoT-based Smart Water Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper presents PipeBeGood, an in-telligent water quality monitoring (WQM) system for water pipe systems. PipeBeGood leverages real-time multimodal data from cameras, flowmeters, and temperature sensors, along with a hybrid approach for data analysis. It employs a hybrid multimodal data analysis approach with two deep learning-based computer vision models for image analysis and rule-based approaches for flowmeter and temperature data analysis to monitor the state of pipes and their contents. As demonstrated, PipeBeGood can detect irregularities or problems and notify stakeholders accordingly. However, current image recognition models require further training due to the need for live image data with real-life objects within water, such as wet wipes.

articleTitle: Optimation of Convolutional Neural Networks With Hyperparameter to Identification Indonesian Traditional Puppet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to introduce a novel method for classifying Indonesian puppet characters using modified Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Traditional classification methods for these characters, which are crucial to Indonesian cultural heritage, depend significantly on expert knowledge and manual efforts, resulting in time-consuming processes and potential inconsistencies. Our approach utilizes deep learning techniques to automate the identification process, thus improving both accuracy and efficiency. We developed and trained a modified CNN model on a dataset containing images of eight unique Wayang characters: Arjuna, Bima, and Gatotkaca. Furthermore, we optimized the CNN model using hyperparameter tuning to enhance its performance and reliability in character classification. The model was evaluated on its ability to classify these characters, achieving an overall test accuracy of 77.29%. The classification results demonstrate notable performance, with precision, recall, and F1-score metrics for each character as follows: Arjuna (precision 0.69, recall 0.76, F1-score 0.73), Bima (precision 0.79, recall 0.88, F1-score 0.83), Gatotkaca (precision 0.75, recall 0.79, F1-score 0.77), Kresna (precision 0.71, recall 0.83, F1-score 0.77), Puntadewa (precision 0.77, recall 0.80, F1-score 0.78), Sengkuni (precision 0.82, recall 0.58, F1-score 0.68), and Togog (precision 0.91, recall 0.97, F1-score 0.94). The model's macro average precision, recall, and F1-score are 0.79, 0.78, and 0.78, while the weighted average metrics are all 0.77.

articleTitle: Harnessing GAN to Create Realistic FBS(False Base Station) Attack Data in 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The threat of false base stations (FBS) has evolved with the advancement of mobile communication, posing severe risks in the 5G era. FBSs can mimic legitimate stations, leading to various malicious activities like man-in-the-middle attacks, denial-of-service attacks, and spreading fake disaster messages. Detecting FBSs is crucial, but existing methods relying on machine learning face challenges due to insufficient datasets. To address this, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are explored to augment limited datasets by generating realistic data. This paper investigates using GANs to enhance datasets for FBS detection, compares the similarity between generated and real datasets, and assesses detection accuracy. Furthermore, we trained machine learning models on GAN-generated data and utilized it to implement an FBS detection Network Function (NF) for 5G environments. Ultimately, we generated a dataset with a high similarity, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.85, using GAN s. We confirmed the possibility of utilizing this dataset for FBS detection and applied it in a 5G environment.

articleTitle: RGBD Depth Sensor Frame Data Streaming to Handheld Device Using WebRTC-Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Depth estimation on handheld devices can be highly beneficial for enhancing Augmented Reality (AR) applications. Depth estimation enables spatial awareness functionalities for a more realistic and immersive environment in the application such as occlusion handling, collision detection, and lighting. These improvements allow AR applications more engaging and practical, opening up new possibilities for education, navigation, gaming, and various other fields. However, performing depth estimation on handheld devices requires high computational processing. This paper presents a method to live stream RGBD depth sensor frame data to browsers in handheld devices using a WebRTCbased framework, therefore bypassing the device's computational limitations. The WebRTC-based framework also allows transmission on input from users like tapping the screen, thus the application can be controlled in real time as well. We detailed the flow and implemented the method using Unity Render Streaming and ZED Mini depth sensor, demonstrating successful depth estimation and occlusion handling in an AR application. The results show that when the occlusion handling toggle is turned on, the depth of the scene is understood by the AR application and the virtual objects were correctly occluded by the real object, in which we use hand gestures. The hand gestures consist of open palm and grabbing gestures. The research concludes that the WebRTC-based Unity Render Streaming framework can effectively integrate depth sensors with handheld devices that support HTML5 browsers, offering a new pathway for immersive AR experiences. The method is also robust with different depth sensors, as long as the depth sensor's camera feed can be displayed by the Unity game engine.

articleTitle: Evaluations of Distinct Bitonic Sorters for ORBGRAND
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Guessing Random Additive Noise Decoding (GRAND) is a recently proposed decoding algorithm for forward error correction codes in fifth-generation (5G) consumer communications. Order Reliability Bits GRAND (ORBGRAND) was proposed to utilize received channel values and sort all of them to get more probable error patterns. Therefore, choosing an efficient algorithm to sort the channel values significantly influences the hardware design of the ORBGRAND. In this study, different bitonic sorters are evaluated in terms of frame error rate, synthesized silicon area, and power consumption. To achieve a low-cost ORBGRAND, the half-output bitonic sorter with segmentation not only reduces the number of the compare and swap unit, but also reduces number of the pipeline register. The evaluation results show that the half-output bitonic sorter with two segmentation can achieve 38% area reduction and 39% power reduction, respectively.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Optimization of MobileNet Architecture on Balinese Mask Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study utilized MobileN et to surpass the accuracy of previous research in the field of Balinese mask image classification. Balinese masks as one of the objects of Balinese cultural heritage must be preserved. Based on the data collected, most of young generation in Bali who has no interest in Balinese masks. The approach in the field of technology is known to have a very effective impact on the younger generation because of its rapid and efficient deployment. To improve accuracy, we analyze hyperparameter combinations such as learning rate, batch size, and dropout. Based on 16 scenarios, we got an accuracy of 98.57% for the combination of learning rate 0.00001, batch size 8, and dropout 40%. This value exceeds previous studies using the VGG16 architecture with an accuracy of 85%.

articleTitle: Development Framework for Web-Based Multi-Location 360VR Videos Supporting VR Goggles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper treats development frameworks for web-based VR contents of 360VR images/videos. Recently, many companies produce VR goggles and many game companies release VR games that support VR goggles. However, there are few educational VR contents. Also, many companies produce 360VR cameras. It can be said that 360VR contents of 360VR images/videos supporting VR goggles are useful for education purposes, e.g., in the experiment or exercise subjects, students can deeply learn how they perform the experiments or exercises beforehand by experience of the 360VR contents. To easily develop such 360VR contents, the authors have already proposed several development frameworks for web-based VR contents such as navigation contents of 360VR videos and walkthrough contents of 360VR images. In this paper, the authors propose new development framework for web-based multi-location 360VR videos supporting VR goggles. There have been many services of freeviewpoint videos and free-viewpoint live streaming videos. However, there are not any multi-location 360VR videos. Multi-location 360VR videos supporting VR goggles have higher immersion rather than normal 360VR videos and freeviewpoint videos. So, multi-location 360VR videos supporting VR goggles are useful for education purposes. The authors insist the usefulness of the proposed development framework by showing several multi-location 360VR videos supporting VR goggles actually developed using the framework.

articleTitle: Emotional Recognition of Netizens Voice Message on Social Media by using Deep Learning Neural Network Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Communication activities between netizens represent the condition of curiosity to find out new information through social media such as Telegram, Line or WhatsApp. This has made the style response in the speaking process and represents the emotional condition. In this research, speech emotions were identified in Indonesian through voice notes on social media, especially WhatsApp. The speech is analyzed and classified to determine the conditional emotions of Indonesian netizens. The step started with composed the sound of audio dataset to the form of a file (mono.wav) and carried out by feature extraction using the Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) and classified by using the Deep Learning Neural Network. The classifier in this case is 1D Convolutional Neural Network with Swish Net architecture. System testing indicated a good performance on kernel 6 epoch 100, with output precision in the form of identifying 4 types of emotions Happy (93%), Angry (91%), Neutral (83%), and Sad (100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>).

articleTitle: Study of Reducing Sound Discomfort by Dynamic Range Compression Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Hyperacusis is a symptom of overreaction to certain sounds or excessive loudness of sounds that are not bothersome to normal-hearing people. Countermeasures against hyperacusis include the use of earmuffs or earplugs and moving to a quieter place. However, acoustic protection with earplugs or earmuffs may further deteriorate volume perception with prolonged wear. Therefore, the ultimate goal of this research is to remove the discomfort associated with the sounds that cause hyperacusis while maintaining the volume of the sounds that you want to hear by suppressing the sounds that cause hyperacusis. Focusing on dynamic range compression, which is mainly used in hearing aids, this study proposes a processing method that reduces loud sounds and leaves quiet sounds as they are. As the input audio gets louder, different dynamic range adjustments are made for each of the three frequency bands. Subjective evaluation will be conducted to determine the degree to which the proposed method reduces sound discomfort. Randomize the order and perform A-B evaluation on 5 levels with the RMS values of the processed sound and the original sound matched. The results show that the treated sound is less offensive than the original sound. The study proposed a method of reducing discomfort by dynamic range and demonstrated its effectiveness in subjective evaluation under the condition of matching sound pressure levels.

articleTitle: Enhancing Programming Learning Environment with Augmented Reality Smart Glasses: A Blended Learning Approach for IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study aims to develop an AR smart glasses-assisted IoT learning system that integrates hands-on operation with knowledge acquisition to provide a more immersive blended learning environment, enhancing learners' focus on creative tasks. The educational framework, developed using Unity and Epson Moverio BT-40 glasses as the learning tool, allows learners to effectively receive guidance and learning content without altering their viewpoint. Testing with 15 university students revealed improved learning outcomes despite a dependent samples T-test yielding a non-statistically significant p-value of 0.329. Student feedback indicates high interactivity and autonomy in the learning process. However, further improvement is needed in object recognition sensitivity and the variety of instructional video controls.

articleTitle: A Study of Video Games in Handgrip Exergame System for Hypertension Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Nowadays, hypertension or high blood pressure is the highest risk for the health of a lot of people. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that about 1.28 billion people at 30-79 years old are suffering from it. Unfortunately, people often may not be unaware of hypertension until it becomes too late. Handgrip exercises using a foam ball has been known as an effective method to reduce blood pressure. Therefore, we have studied an exergame system to encourage handgrip exercises by playing video games. The system is implemented on a personal computer with a camera in Python using Mediapipe to recognize the handgrip gestures to control the game. In this paper, we investigate proper video games that can be installed in this system. We list the conditions of them and show sample video games satisfying them that can be downloaded from the Internet. The validity evaluations will be in future works.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Graph Neural Networks for Device Classification in Social IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The Social Internet of Things (SIoT) integrates the principles of social networks with the Internet of Things, enabling devices to interact based on social relationships. The information network produced from such connectivity has shown efficient query processing and collaborative tasks. Motivated by these characteristics and prospects of such a compiled relationship, this work studies the construction of a graph-compatible dataset from a public IoT platform's access records for device classification. The proposed graph-formatted dataset-building process utilises a two-level time-based approach. The first level uses a time-based resampling mechanism for graph definition, while the second one exploits nodes' historical co-location records for functional connectivity. Following the dataset construction, this work studies the performance of Graph Neural Networks (GNN) to predict a device type by employing two operators for node classification problems, e.g., Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and GraphSAGE. Our results show that models utilised both graph operators achieve satisfactory results, with an accuracy ≥ 0.8 and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F1-\mathbf{score }\geq 0.7$</tex> on validation and test sets defined.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Bit-Flip Attacks on Extreme Learning Machine for Age-related Macular Degeneration Detection on OCT Volumes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In recent years, the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) architecture has been widely applied in various fields, leading to an increase in hardware attack attempts. However, the security challenges of ELM weights have not been thoroughly studied. This study investigates the impact of bit-flip attacks (BFA) on ELM, focusing on the different weights and the importance of each bit position within these weights. We employed two strategies: random BFA and indexed random BFA. These attacks were used to assess their effects on the accuracy of ELM models. In the random BFA, attacking the input weight caused a 1.87% accuracy drop for each bit attacked. Attacking the output weight resulted in a 50.44<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy drop after five bits were attacked. Based on the indexed random BFA results, we recommend protecting the first seven bits of the input weight and the first twenty bits of the output weight.

articleTitle: The Design of Aurel's with Artificial Intelligence Learning Based on Deep Learning for Autism Pervasive Development Disorder Children
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Pervasive developmental disorder or Autism Pervasive Development Disorder (APDD) is a disorder with psychomotor, cognitive, sensory, interpersonal, and intrapersonal conditions that are expected to tend to experience delays or not develop appropriately during childhood. Around 58.7 per 10,000 children in Indonesia experience pervasive developmental disorders. Children with pervasive disorders cannot interact well with others. They tend to be attracted to various inanimate objects, due to severe communication limitations and strong obsessive desires. A neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by a lack of social interaction, social interaction (verbal and nonverbal), and repetitive behavior or restricted interests is commonly called pervasive autism. developmental disorder (APDD). Many researchers and doctors have developed autism treatments by teaching children with APPD several approaches or methods to develop their social and mental skills, including the use of technology. Aurel's study (Autism Robotics Experience for Learners) is based on deep-based artificial intelligence applications learning so that the robot can be directly controlled for movement and audio-visual systems. Aurel was developed to provide interventions for children on the autism spectrum (APDD). Aurel's is designed to create movements and sounds that help children with APPD develop social skills. Aurel matches the characteristics of autistic children (APDD), has eyesight, and likes technology. In doing so, Aurel uses an early intervention method or approach. Early intervention is therapy for children from birth to 3 years of age for children with special needs and growth and development disorders. Aurel can carry out activities to observe the development of early childhood children to optimize skills according to their needs.

articleTitle: A Work-Suitability Score Calculation System for a Sustainable Human Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation method for a “work-suitability score” calculation system for the purpose of realizing an optimal staffing system based on workers” skills., availability., aptitudes and preferences for the assigned work and tasks. Specifically., our system firstly calculates the available working hours., secondary allocates workers based on logic., and thirdly actively reallocates workers based on the work-suitability score. In recent years., it is expected that both the elimination of uneven working hours and the improvement of efficiency and productivity are realized together. Our system is characterized by the fact that mathematical optimization is used to meet the need for increased efficiency in administrative work and to implement the goal of improving worker“s satisfaction as a solution to the problem of unbalanced working hours and unmatching skills. By using this system., managers in the personnel department become able to clearly grasp the bias of working hours and enterprises realize a sustainable human resource allocation.

Author Keywords: SDGs8 Decent Work and Economic Growth

articleTitle: Analysis and Control of Ammunition Transportation Risk Management at Explosive Storage Depots and Consumer (User Units) in the Indonesian Navy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The risk of ammunition transportation in explosive storage warehouses is very high, making safety and security management essential, considering potential impacts such as injury and fatality. This research aims to analyze the risks associated with ammunition transportation in storage warehouses, both active and expired, at the Naval Storage Depot. Transportation plays a crucial role in moving ammunition from one warehouse to another for storage rotation or readiness for consumer by the user units. So far trucks have been considered faster and more effective for transportation, but significant hazards such as shocks, impacts, vibrations, and road conditions increase the negative risks to ammunition, such as ammunition damage, chemical degradation due to shocks and vibrations, or gas leaks. In the past the use of trolley had a high safety level but practical constraints like transportation routes made them less feasible leading to their deactivation due to situational demands. Risk analysis is conducted through a systematic approach that includes identification, assessment, control, and risk management in the use of transportation tools between trucks and trolleys. This comparison is expected to control risk management and decision- making to provide an understanding of potential risks and the development of effective mitigation strategies contributing to improved safety and security during ammunition transportation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) Filter Performance for GPS Anti-Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The act of deliberately directing electromagnetic energy towards a communication and/or navigation system with the purpose to interrupt or inhibit signal transmission and reception is known as jamming. Jamming is used to send high signal to disrupt the Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) communication and force the UAVs to land. This prevents the operator from receiving UAV, which results in the UAV losing control. Jamming activity may present a substantial threat to the communication security of the country especially for military. A Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) filter is the alternative option to mitigate jamming activity. The FSS filter has several benefits such as effective performance in term of having high bandwidth and high transmission, low-cost and lightweight material which is suitable to be implemented for UAVs. In this paper, we investigate the performance of proposed FSS bandpass filter using Ansys software simulation at 2.4 GHz. The Ansys Software is used to design the band pass filter in a simple square shape by varying several parameters such as element length (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>), width of aperture (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b$</tex>) and periodic length (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex>). A complete design and analysis of the proposed FSS square filter is based on the reflection coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and transmission coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> are presented in this paper. The transmission of the filter is 97%. In conclusion, the proposed dimension of the square unit cell that can filter out the jamming signal for small UAV size is 38 mm, aperture width is 2.9 mm and the periodic length is 60 mm.

articleTitle: Cloud-Connected Human-Drone Interface for Intuitive Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: As drone technologies become more abundant, efficient and robust, path planning has become increasingly necessary. For ease of use, Human-Machine Interaction (HMI) applications have been developed to simplify the user experience and ensure efficient navigation. These applications enhance the drone's ability to perform various tasks, such as surveillance, delivery, and photography, with reliability and precision. This paper presents an innovative Human-Drone-Interface (HDI) designed to simplify the navigation of drones along user-defined paths. Drone flight paths can be defined by drawing routes or specifying Points of Interest (POIs) on a digital map, streamlining the user experience for users. This work addresses the hardware and software challenges of interpreting user-defined paths in real time, optimizing the drone's route, and generating precise flight commands. Algorithmic computations are delegated to the cloud to enhance battery efficiency. The system incorporates the Long Range (LoRa) protocol to communicate with the drone, which enables a more extended range of operations while providing reliable connectivity in areas with poor coverage and limited broadband access. By making drones easier to operate, the proposed solution seeks to make drones more widely accessible, thus pushing the boundaries of user-friendly drone navigation. Testing results demonstrated the HDI's robust ability to consistently instruct drones along user-defined paths. This capability makes it well-suited for real-world applications such as agriculture, where precise navigation is essential for irrigation or delivery systems, where path optimization ensures timely delivery of nackages.

articleTitle: Deepfake Face Images: Explainable Detection using Deep Neural Networks and Class Activation Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Our study presents an improved method for detecting deepfake content using advanced explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques. We focused on enhancing deep neural networks, specifically Residual Network (ResNet) models such as ResNet50V2, ResNet101V2, and ResNet152V2, with Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to more accurately differentiate between real and artificial faces. The addition of XAI principles through Grad-CAM not only increases the detection accuracy but also makes the decision-making process of the models transparent, fostering trust, and making the technology more accessible for real-world applications. We evaluated our models using the FFHQ dataset, which comprises a vast array of real and fake facial images. The results demonstrated significant improvements in both precision and recall rates across all models with the integration of Grad-CAM. Specifically, the enhanced ResNet50V2 model achieved a precision of 87% for fake images and 94% for real images, with recall rates of 94% for fake images and 86% for real images, resulting in f1 scores of 90% for both classes. The ResNet101V2 and ResNet152V2 models with Grad-CAM also showed notable improvements, with the ResNet101V2 + Grad-CAM model reaching a precision of 87% for fake and 96% for real, and the ResNet152V2 + Grad-CAM model achieving a precision of 90% for fake and 92% for real, both with high recall and f1 scores, highlighting the precision and reliability of the method. Our approach not only addresses the challenge of detecting deepfakes with high accuracy but also balances the model complexity with computational efficiency. Despite some limitations, such as data set biases and occasional misclassifications, our method significantly advances digital media authentication and shows promising prospects for identity and security verification. Future work will focus on refining these models, emphasizing the importance of XAI, and exploring their application to broader image-classification challenges to strengthen defenses against the evolving threat of deepfake technology.

articleTitle: A Proposal of Concurrent Exercise Monitoring System using Multiple Wearable Heart Rate Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Conventional methods of monitoring exercise have mostly focused on individual athletes, neglecting the importance of simultaneously tracking several athletes participating in group workouts. Nowadays, with the advancement of consumer technology and IoT, it becomes possible to simultaneously monitor a group of athletes' performance. To address this gap, we propose a concurrent real-time exercise monitoring. The system adopts multiple commercial wearable heart rate sensors communicating with a single-board computer via Bluetooth low-energy (BLE). We outline the design and functionality of the proposed system, emphasizing its potential applications in team sports training and performance optimization. The results on the functionality and received signal strength indicator (RSSI) test on a group of people in a gym facility show the feasibility of the system. By concurrently monitoring the heart rate data of multiple athletes, we aim to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of exercise monitoring, specifically targeting the needs of group athletes and their respective sports teams.

articleTitle: Implementation of Augmented Reality on Traditional Sikut Satak Architecture in Balinese Traditional Houses Based on Android
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) is a technology that combines virtual objects with the real world and gives users the experience of feeling an object virtually. In its discussion, it will be used to visualize traditional sikut satak architecture in today's era, which is said to be difficult to apply. This is because the concept of sikut satak in Balinese traditional houses requires fairly large land, which includes the core building, based on the direction of the wind. Because these buildings are an architectural unity worthy of being called karang sikut satak. This situation and obstacles become problems and impact the abandonment of this traditional concept. In Balinese society today, it is felt to be shifting towards modern architecture, which is considered simpler and has more minimal costs to build a house. The purpose of this research is to make information media about traditional sikut satak architecture into augmented reality media with an Android operating system. This step is an effort to preserve the architecture of Balinese houses called sikut satak, as well as a means of providing information on the archipelago's cultural heritage. The feature displays information on traditional components and elements in a virtual experience. The implication is proven that the black box testing user experience application testing resulted in 86% stating very good or criteria worthy of supporting the mission carried and can continue to be developed in the future as an effort to preserve traditional culture

Author Keywords: sikut satak. architecture balinese traditional houses

articleTitle: Empowering Skill-Based Learning with Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper presents a case study on the implementation of Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) technologies in skill-based learning. We discuss our experience in leveraging these technologies to create an immersive, interactive and engaging learning experience for skill-based learning that is not limited to laboratory setting and is able to reach a wider audience. Our findings suggest that AR and VR learning modules significantly enhance the understanding and retention of skills among learners. We also explore the challenges faced during implementation and provide insights into how they can be effectively addressed. Furthermore, we discuss the positive feedback received from both the instructors and the learners, underscoring the effectiveness of these technologies in enhancing learning outcomes and learner engagement. The paper concludes with lessons learned from our experience and areas of future work, contributing to the ongoing discussions on the use of AR and VR technologies in education.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation and Industry 4.0 in Indonesian Shipyards (Case Study at PT PAL Indonesia)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Digital transformation and Industry 4.0 have proven to be capable of strengthening corporate performance, creating value, and gaining competitive advantage in various industries. Its appeal has increased among companies from various sectors and government agencies in the Indonesian economy, but limited generalizability and replicability have been found in existing models, which poses difficulties in applicability to the Indonesian shipbuilding industry. Therefore, this research study aims to identify and analyze PT PAL Indonesia's implementation of industry 4.0 principles including the impact of digital transformation and implementation on production processes and overall company performance and the main challenges faced in industry 4.0 transformation. In this study using mixed methods with qualitative and quantitative analysis to collect data from surveys/ questionnaires and also company data. The results of simultaneous testing research (F test) shows the simultaneous influence of the application of industrial transformation 4.0 on the achievement of organizational goals. The test results are shown in the financial performance of PT PAL Indonesia's RKAP which experienced a significant increase from 2020 worth Rp. 1,826 billion to Rp. 3,620 billion in 2023 and projections in 2024 reached Rp. 5,109 billion. In terms of productivity capabilities, it has also increased from 20 ship blocks per month to 50 ship blocks per month, which of course has an impact on shorter dock time and faster shipbuilding time. However, the challenges faced in implementing industry 4.0 are related to culture and openness to change. In addition, there are also investment costs for infrastructure provision and human resource development.

articleTitle: Digital Twin System for Smart Buildings Integrated with Blockchain and Mixed Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The integration of 3D innovation, Mixed Reality (MR), and blockchain in smart buildings has revolutionized the IoT sector. Visualization using 3D technology and immersive interfaces allows users to control and interact with devices within smart building environments. Users can use hand gestures or controllers in a 3D environment to adjust lighting, monitor energy consumption, or manage other smart devices. When combined with MR, the capabilities of 3D technology are enhanced with virtual elements overlaying onto the real-world environment. Within smart buildings, MR can visualize real-time sensor data, display device statuses, and provide intuitive visual feedback. The integration of blockchain in this ecosystem adds layers of security, transparency, and trust by securely recording and verifying device data, control commands, and user interactions. Blockchain technology enables secure peer-to-peer communication and smart contracts for automated device interactions and control. User testing results for controlling smart buildings with Mixed Reality (MR) technology showed high user satisfaction with an average score of 4.48. Users appreciated the performance and functionality of the system, as well as the new experience provided by the natural and immersive MR interface for interacting with smart building controls.

articleTitle: ERP Platform for Supply Chain Operational System using LoRa and Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The industry is an important pillar in reducing unemployment in a country and improving the well-being of the country's population. Based on data from the Ministry of Industry stated that about 60% of the absorption of the unemployed population comes from the industrial sector. Indonesia has a fairly stable growth of the industrial sector based on data in 2024. Based on data from the Ministry of Industry stated that about 60% of the absorption of the unemployed population comes from the industrial sector. Indonesia has a fairly stable growth of the industrial sector based on data in 2021. Enterprise Resource Planning is a platform created for the purpose of managing the operational processes of the supply chain. Using ERP, companies improved performance through efficiency, administrative automation, and performance in business processes. With high data change activity integrated with ERP. This requires a system that guaranteed data security and is permanent or changed by any party. We Purposed ERP platform that could be connected to LoRa - Blockchain, which improved efficiency in supply chain delivery, strengthen data security on the platform, and increase user confidence with decentralized data storage. The results of this study with LoRa as a vehicle GPS data sender communication already deliver data location with errors up to less then 1% and the data is already saved in blockchain.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality-Based Navigation: Bridging Indoor and Outdoor Environments through Immersal Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: A navigation system is an essential tool designed to assist users in determining and following a route from one location to another. Navigation systems are typically categorized into two types: outdoor navigation systems designed for open areas and indoor navigation systems used within enclosed spaces. However, transitioning between indoor and outdoor environments has limitations, often requiring users to switch applications, such as using GPS for outdoor navigation and a different application for indoor navigation. Therefore, we propose the integration of indoor and outdoor navigation based on Augmented Reality. The development of AR navigation system begins with the creation of 3D assets of the Politeknik Elektronika Negeri Surabaya (PENS) campus, which is the site of our research including three buildings for indoor navigation and the connecting roads between the buildings for outdoor navigation. The development of this navigation system uses the Immersal SDK as a library for Spatial Mapping, Localization and System Integration. Several features are included, such as indoor-outdoor navigation, multilevel floor navigation, and zero additional devices. The system testing results are based on user testing, integration testing, and multilevel floor testing. From User Testing with PIECES Framework, 32 respondents expressed satisfaction with the proposed system. Integration Testing showed that the system could navigate between indoor and outdoor environments. And Multilevel Floor Testing demonstrated that the system could navigate within buildings with multiple floors.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Impact Analysis of Requirement Changes using LLM in Software Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The software industry is continuously evolving because of emerging technologies, evolving development methodologies, changing business needs, and shifting stakeholder preferences. Effectively managing daily changes is critical, especially given the complexity of requirement change management (RCM), which requires the development of adaptable systems that accurately reflect dynamic conditions. This paper explores the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically GPT-4, into software engineering to enhance the effectiveness of RCM. This paper proposes a novel methodology that leverages the sophisticated reasoning capabilities of LLM GPT-4 to analyze and predict the impacts of software requirement changes before implementation. Our approach combines LLMs with a structured analysis framework that interprets changes in software requirements and evaluates their potential impacts across multiple dimensions. The use of GPT-4 can revolutionize how software engineers understand and implement requirements changes, providing a comprehensive tool for predicting the impact of such changes and evaluating the consequences accurately. The results of this research can help requirements engineers perform automated change impact analysis, enabling them to make informed decisions regarding the acceptance or rejection of requirement change requests. This ultimately supports the creation of software products that better align with consumer needs and expectations, ensuring enhanced user experiences and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Private Blockchain-Based Platform for Cool Box Truck Based on LoRa Communication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things utilizes software, embedded system, sensor, and network connectivity to control and monitor business processes such as supply chains. One of the implementations of IoT is LoRa (Long Range) which enables data transactions in long-range without using radio frequency. Currently, a combination of IoT and blockchain is able to increase the security level of IoT applications. Implementation of IoT in the supply chain has been done in several research by implementing blockchain and LoRa. Approximately 6.43% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is attributed to logistics, with cold and hot logistics constituting around 11%. Among these, cold chain logistics, a specialized form, accounts for 9.7% of tonnage. Cold chain logistics, characterized by comprehensive temperature control, is a sophisticated system closely intertwined with advanced technology. Despite its complexity, there are still technological drawbacks leading to significant material losses on an annual basis. In this research, to overcome that problem, we proposed Blockchain-Based Monitoring System on Cool Box Trucks using LoRa.
