The proposed system implemented LoRa for data communication and Blockchain as decentralized databases. We simulated the LoRa environment by using FLoRa framework to obtain the optimal parameters such as Transmission Power (TP), Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), and Spread Factor (SF) that used in TTGO T-Beam V1.

articleTitle: Optimizing AI-Based Sign Language Technologyby Overcoming the Limitations of Two-Way Communication for Deaf People Through Community Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Over the years, the world has rapidly developed in all aspects, such as social, cultural, economic, artistic, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been used in life, especially in the aspect of communication in everyday life. The development of a device and software that is integrated, will make it easier for deaf and hearing people to communicate effectively. However, currently, the development of sign language technology tends to use smart gloves, so this raises questions about the efficiency of using technology in sign language development. In addition, there arestill limitations in collecting sign language vocabulary data, so the use of the technology is not maximized. Based on the problems above, we offer two solutions, first, developing sign language technology using Artificial Intelligence (AI) which only uses a cellphone camera and records movements without hardware will be more effective and efficient. Second, the author offers a solution, like the setting of inputting sign vocabulary data using community participation in each region of the world. Thus, the sign language vocabulary will increase and the communication process can be performed optimally.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Education and Tourism: Scholarly Trends and Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the intersection between education and tourism, examining 875 publications from 2013 to 2023 sourced from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. Utilizing co-citation, co-authorship, and keyword co-occurrence techniques, the study maps the intellectual landscape of this field. Key findings reveal a substantial increase in research output, largely propelled by advancements in digital technologies such as virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), which enhance educational tourism through immersive experiences. The major themes identified include sustainable tourism education, experiential learning, and the role of technology in improving educational outcomes. The analysis also highlights influential authors, institutions, and journals within the field. Emerging trends point to a growing emphasis on sustainability in tourism curricula and an increased application of VR and AR. These insights provide valuable guidance for educators, researchers, and policymakers, underscoring the dynamic nature of the field and the evolving educational practices driven by technological advancements. The study emphasizes the critical role of education in tourism and offers a roadmap for future research and collaboration in this evolving domain.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Traditional Machine Learning and Quantum Computing in Natural Language Processing: A Case Study on Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This research paper primarily investigates the application and performance of traditional machine learning and quantum computing in Natural Language Processing (NLP), with a focus on sentiment analysis tasks. By comparing the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of these two technologies, the study aims to reveal the potential of quantum computing in handling complex NLP tasks and to provide data support for future technology choices and research directions. The paper also details the use of 1M DB and NLTK movie review datasets for experiments and discusses the experimental design, performance evaluation results, and technical challenges faced by both methods.

articleTitle: Real-time Monitoring Using AWS Cloud Platform For Agriculture Soil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In the era of modern agriculture, real-time monitoring of soil conditions is crucial for increasing productivity and efficiency. This research proposes an agricultural soil monitoring system that utilizes the AWS Cloud platform to capture, analyze, and present real-time soil data. This system is designed to integrate various sensors that can measure humidity, pH, temperature and soil nutrients, all connected via the Internet of Things (IoT). The data collected by these sensors is sent to the AWS Cloud, where it is processed using cloud computing services such as AWS Lambda and Amazon EC2. The use of the AWS Cloud enables high scalability, reliability, and data security, and facilitates big data analysis using Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. By using an intuitive dashboard, farmers can see soil analysis results in real-time and make informed decisions based on the data. Additionally, this system is equipped with machine learning algorithms that run on the AWS Cloud to predict soil needs and provide optimal fertilizer recommendations. This research shows how implementing AWS Cloud in agriculture can bring digital transformation to agriculture, enabling farmers to increase crop yields while reducing waste and operational costs.

articleTitle: Strategies for Advancing Hub Ports to Boost International Container Ship Trade in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In international trade, the distribution of goods via sea freight, particularly container ships, remains irreplaceable. There are multiple options to route cargoes (containers) from the port of loading (POL) to the port of destination (POD). The use of container shipping in Indonesia is increasingly evolving. Indonesia, as a major country with a strategic location in Asia, still depends on foreign hub ports for international container ship routes. Establishing a hub port in Indonesia is constrained by various factors, both technical and regulatory. This article offers a scenario analysis approach to explore various potential strategies for developing a hub port in Indonesia. This research aims to assess the development strategy for hub ports in Indonesia. The results of this study indicate that Jakarta is ready to be developed as a hub to attract larger vessels or direct services. However, vessel operators face difficulties in fulfilling the minimum volume (TEUs) on their direct service (big vessel). Collecting cargo (containers) from surrounding ports also faces several obstacles. One of the obstacles was trainway connectivity, as they were connected to Surabaya port, but not to Jakarta port. Another issue is that shipping lines cannot optimize the use of their vessels to collect containers from Semarang and Surabaya going to Jakarta because of the cabotage principal. This study is expected to serve as a reference for stakeholders in developing their business strategies and for the government in future regulatory formulation and implementation.

articleTitle: Transformation to Enhance Business Resilience In Construction Companies: Systematic Literature Review Of Dimensional Models *
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Improving business resilience in construction companies is crucial because of the sector's vulnerability to various risks and disruptions. Enhancing resilience enables construction firms to better withstand and recover from challenges such as natural disasters, economic downturns, and pandemics like COVID-19. This study aims to identify and analyze the key dimensions of business resilience in construction companies and to develop a comprehensive framework for enhancing resilience. This study used a systematic literature review approach guided by the Preferred Reposting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA). Based on the literature review that has been carried out, the dimensions of the transformation, and business resilience variables consist of several dimensions. This research contributes to existing knowledge by identifying critical dimensions that define business resilience specifically in the context of construction companies. This identification helps in understanding the unique challenges and needs for resilience in this industry so that a framework can be created.

articleTitle: Exploring Energy Harvesting: A Study on Triboelectric Nanogenerators Based on Vertical Contact-Separation Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The growing demand for energy-efficient and self-sufficient devices is driving increased interest in energy harvesting solutions, as the frequent replacement and disposal of batteries contributes to environmental pollution. This has prompted experts to explore sustainable and renewable energy sources. Triboelectric nanogenerators, which convert mechanical motion into electrical energy, are emerging as a promising technology for energy harvesting. This can be achieved by pairing two materials with different triboelectric properties. The aim was to generate voltage and current in a vertical contact-separation mode triboelectric nanogenerator (CS-TENG) using three different configurations. This project utilized polyester, nylon, and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) as dielectric materials and aluminum (Al) foil as conductors of the triboelectric pairs. CS-TENGs work by contacting and separating two materials by hand tapping with and without latex gloves, with one material gaining electrons and the other losing electrons. The output voltage and current were measured using a digital multimeter and an oscilloscope. The simple and cost-effective CS-TENGs exhibit an average output voltage of 23 V, an output current of 3.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> with an oscillation frequency of 2 Hz. In addition, it is also capable of illuminating the five LED arrays without a rectifier circuit. The storage capability was stored in a 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{F}$</tex> capacitor, and the green LED was powered up using the stored energy. This study can contribute to the comprehension of how CS-TENGs can be engineered and improved to facilitate their potential application in practical energy harvesting generation and wearable electronics technology.

articleTitle: Recovery Improvement at the West Block Screening Station of Nickel Mining through the Integration of Six Sigma and Sologic Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Screening recovery, measured as the ratio of Screen Station Product (SSP) to the Run-of-Mine (ROM) ore fed, significantly declined by 16%, from 60% to 50%, during 2017–2021. This research addresses this decline by identifying root causes and proposing improvement steps using a combination of the Six Sigma method and the Sologic method. The Six Sigma method, which follows the DMAIC cycle (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control), was used to systematically identify and address process inefficiencies, while the Sologic method was employed for root cause analysis. Ten primary causes with high to moderate risk levels were identified and categorized into transitory, non-transitory, and omission types using the Sologic method. Three improvement steps involving substitution, engineering technology, and administrative control were implemented, focusing on transitory causes. Based on validated causes, improvement plans focused on recycling reject material, enhancing tramming activities, and refreshing dumping procedures through operator training to improve recovery and minimize carryover. Recycling reject material successfully increased the daily recycled material from 118 to 591 tonnes, while enhancing tramming activities raised trammed material from 10,396 to 11,473 tonnes/day. These improvements increased screening station recovery from 50% to 59% and raised the sigma value from 3.46 to 4.60. Continuous monitoring through the Floor Management Development System (FMDS) and gemba activities ensured the effectiveness and consistency of these changes.

articleTitle: Designing a Web-based Babysitting Service Business in Jakarta Using Design Thinking Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The increasing demands of modern lifestyles and career responsibilities, especially among working women, have led to a growing need for childcare services in Jakarta. This research aims to design a web-based babysitting service business in Jakarta using a design thinking approach. The research methodology follows the five stages of design thinking: empathise, define, ideate, prototype, and test. The business model is designed with a ten types of innovation approach to overcome the limitations of conventional childcare services. The service prototype is a web-based babysitting service offering two main services: Daycare and Go Nanny. The prototype was tested using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ). The UEQ results are: attractiveness is 2.341, perspicuity is 2.262, efficiency is 2.310, dependability is 2.250, stimulation is 2.274, and novelty is 2.071. This results falls within the excellent category, indicating that the web-based babysitting service prototype meets user expectations.

articleTitle: Self-learning Model for Node.js-based Backend Web Programming Featuring Automatic Source Code Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The significance of web applications has grown immensely due to the widespread availability of the internet and their extensive usage across various devices. Currently, Node.js emerged as the most extensively embraced web framework among software developers worldwide. As a result, there is a high demand for skilled web programmers capable of developing Node.js-based web applications. Node.js allows web application development using JavaScript on the server side, making it suitable for real-time applications like collaborative tools, online games, and chat applications. This paper presents a self-learning model for Node.js-based web programming that incorporates test-driven development (TDD), leveraging automated testing with Jest and Supertest for code verification. The Basic Web Interface topic within this model requires students to create web elements like headers and paragraphs for personal information display, accompanied by test codes for step-by-step source code verification. Evaluation results from 40 first-year university students indicate successful completion of assignments within varying timeframes and positive feedback on the learning model's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Brand Love Enhancement of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises in Indonesia: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This preliminary paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to explore how consumer brand love of Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSME) in Indonesia could be enhanced through branding strategies. MSMEs play important role in current Indonesia economic growth, but unfortunately, they focus on the trading and forget about the branding. It also examines previous research to observe what should be highligted about brand love, how to identify the variables of the consumer voices and if the latent consumer voices has been identified. To collect the literature data, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar were used as databases. There is a contradictive thing about the masstige brand and MSME's brands about brand love, brand loyalty and purchase intention. Some recommendations strategies could be determined such as good collaboration between the government and MSMEs, and how to gather the latent consumer voice. For further research could be suggested to include interview that would be converted to text document.

articleTitle: Gestational Diabetes Prediction using Machine Learning for Consumer Electronics Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) is a significant health issue t hat affects m any non-diabetic women during pregnancy, with its prevalence steadily increasing. Early and accurate detection of GDM is crucial due to the severe complications it poses for both mothers and their children, including perinatal complications, future diabetes risk, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular issues, pre-eclampsia, and polyhydram-nios. This paper explores the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms for consumer electronics healthcare system to predict GDM, evaluating six models: Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and X G Boost. The dataset includes parameters such as pregnancies, glucose levels, blood pressure, skin thickness, insulin levels, BMI, diabetes pedigree function, age, and outcome, aimed at optimizing prediction accuracy. Through detailed exper-imentation, these models are assessed based on accuracy, mean squared error, R-squared, and root mean square error, presenting the results visually for improved under-standing. By integrating ML into consumer electronics healthcare devices, this approach aims to enhance GDM prediction and management, offering more informed clinical decisions and accessible health monitoring tools, ultimately improving healthcare outcomes for pregnant women and their children.

articleTitle: Analyzing Affordance of Business Process Management Techniques in Enterprise Resource Planning Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is a software package companies use to support organizational performance. The implementation of ERP is a form of business process automation. However, in many companies in Indonesia, ERP implementation is not considered part of business process management (BPM). This paper uses affordance theory to explore the causes of the disconnect between ERP implementation and BPM. An interpretive case study was conducted in a food distribution company that has implemented ERP and a consulting firm that served as a collaborative partner in the ERP implementation. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews with representatives from both companies and analyzed using open and axial coding. The findings of this study indicate that the company could not see the affordance of BPM techniques when they started the ERP implementation. However, the consulting firm helped them see the affordance of some techniques in automating their business processes. These findings can serve as recommendations for companies to automate their business processes to improve performance.

articleTitle: Review of Transfer Learning Techniques for MRI-based Brain Tumor Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Transfer learning (TL) techniques are used to segment brain tumor (BT) images using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as our approach. Our goal is to generate well-conditioned and steady segmentation and classification models through the identification of TL techniques with annotated datasets. Our investigation presents a concise summary of the benchmark for BRaTS datasets, which is employed in BTs analysis. The performance parameters that assess segmentation and classification models, like accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, are evaluated. It is also our conclusion that segmenting and classifying BTs using TL is a challenge due to restrictions, inter-pretation requirements, the deficiency of annotated data, model generalization, and clinical translation. The future research must incorporate clinical data, an advanced TL model, and multi-task learning to segment and categorize in different requirements. The results consider the future advanced BT analysis, which promotes the development of an optimal device to improve the health of BT patients. The Xception model has most superior result compared other models and the others high performance are TL-based DL-model; the combined AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and VGG16; EfficientNet-BO; ResNet 50; MnasNet; ResNeXt-101; and DenseNet-169.

articleTitle: The Influence of Leadership and Institutions on the Success of Open-Source ERP Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Technological developments encourage organizations to make strategic changes to adapt to current trends. ERP is a technology implemented by many organizations. However, the high costs of implementing proprietary ERP make organizations look for alternatives to reduce costs using open-source ERP (OS-ERP). To reduce the risk of failure, organizational development needs to pay attention to ERP success factors. Based on previous research, the most dominant success factors in ERP include organizational and managerial. The active role of top management and company policies can influence users to use ERP actively. This research aims to identify success factors in ERP implementation from a leadership and institutional perspective. Two case studies are conducted on textile manufacturing companies implementing OS-ERP in their organizations. Data is collected via interviews with stakeholders directly involved in developing or implementing the open-source ERP system. The analysis found that the influence of institutions and leadership can encourage the success of ERP implementation. Users are encouraged to immediately make a transition from either the manual system or the current system to the new system with Odoo. Due to policies, users must follow all the rules within the organization. Implementation success is demonstrated by ease of user adaptation, level of adoption and user satisfaction with the system.

articleTitle: Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) Performance Assessment Analysis Using the Best- Worst (BW) and Analytic Network Process (ANP) Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Suppliers are essential actors as providers of resources the company needs in a precise, fast, superior and efficient manner. Performance assessment analysis for supplier relationship management (SRM) is an important thing to do. However, in the fast-moving customer goods (FMCG) industry, especially in the object of this research, it still needs to be comprehensive. This research aims to create a performance assessment analysis model for SRM. The research results and practical implications have been described in the results and conclusions of this paper.

articleTitle: A State-of-the-Art Review of Cyber Threat Intelligence Awareness Programs in Mitigating Bank Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The importance of cyber threat intelligence (CTI) in combating the increasing threat of cyber-attacks, particularly in the context of bank ph ish ing, cannot be overstated. This study investigates the integration of CTI in bolstering cybersecurity awareness programs within the banking sector, with the aim of identifying effective strategies for safeguarding financial data. The primary objective of this study is to explore how banks develop and implement CTI-driven awareness initiatives, highlighting best practices, challenges, and opportunities. A systematic literature review (SLR) conducted using the PRISMA methodology was employed to synthesize findings from high-quality relevant literature. Thefindings of this study indicate that CTI can significantly enhance cybersecurity awareness through tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence. Specifically, tactical intelligence involves the collection of indicators of compromise (IoCs), hash values, and malware behaviour descriptions for immediate threat response. Operational intelligence focuses on real-time threat analysis to understand attack mechanisms and improve situational awareness. Strategic intelligence offers long-term security strategies and insights into emerging threats. Integrating a CTI with security information and event management (SIEM) systems enables financial institutions to rapidly identify and address malicious activities, strengthening their cybersecurity defenses to protect their consumers.

articleTitle: Developing a Personalized English Pronunciation Test and Practice App with Automatic Speech Recognition for Engineering Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study presents the development and evaluation of a personalized English pronunciation practice and test app especially for engineering students at Politeknik Elektronika N egeri Surabaya (PENS). Addressing a gap in conventional word-level pronunciation apps, the state of the art is that it offers personalization in which it allows users to input custom texts containing technical vocabulary and passages relevant to their engineering fields. The app highlights performance through metrics like accuracy percentages and word counts. Through an iterative process involving English instructors and programmers, the app's features (N=12) were refined based on pedagogical requirements and user testing with 60 Multimedia Broadcasting Engineering students. Black-box testing revealed 83.3 % of features functioned as intended. Interviews with 36 students highlighted improvements in pronunciation awareness (73%) and fluency (67.6%), but 40.5% encountered challenges maintaining accuracy with longer text. The research result aligns with calls for learner-centered approaches to language instruction while addressing the unique needs of engineering students in vocational higher education settings. Directions for further research were suggested based on the findings and discussions.

articleTitle: White Matter Lesions Segmentation of FLAIR MRI Based on U-Net Using Cascade Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: White matter lesions (WMLs) are critical neurological markers associated with a range of conditions, including dementia, reduced mobility, and mental health issues. Their prevalence increases with age, making early and accurate detection vital for effective medical intervention. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) serves as a cornerstone in medical imaging for this purpose, particularly using Fluid-Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) sequences. However, the quality of MRI scans can vary due to machine brand, magnetic field strength, and image noise, affecting the accuracy of WMLs segmentation. While existing automated segmentation methods have made strides, they still lag behind expert manual segmentation in terms of accuracy. This paper introduces an innovative approach to WMLs segmentation in FLAIR images using a U-Net architecture enhanced with cascade filtering. Our proposed filtering model employs two filters-Gaussian and Wiener-arranged in serial to improve image quality while preserving essential features. We conducted an ablation study for hyperparameter tuning and compared the performance of our model against three filtering methods and baseline models with no-filtering. Our proposed method not only elevates image quality but also minimizes feature loss, thereby achieving a better Hausdorff distance segmentation score than other models. This research offers a robust and reliable tool for WMLs segmentation, with significant implications for both clinical practice and ongoing research in MRI medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Implementation of Twinguard: Motorcycle Theft Prevention Innovation System with Access Code and Shortest Route Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The increase in the number of motorcycle users in Indonesia increased by 4.39% from 2021 to 2022. This shows that motorcycles are needed by the community. However, along with this increase, the number of theft cases has also increased, especially in densely populated urban areas. The current security system is considered ineffective because it only relies on double locks and alarms. Therefore, we propose the Twinguard system as an Internet of Things (IoT)-based security to prevent motorcycle theft. This system performs theft detection using MPU6050, tracking and monitoring, and the application of Dijkstra's algorithm as a shortest route recommendation feature. The results of this study show that the Twinguard system has an average SMS sending duration of 462 ms. The accuracy difference between Twinguard GPS and smartphone GPS is 2.51 meters, and the GPS only takes 10 seconds to get a satellite signal when outdoors. Then, the access code feature as a vehicle access right can work up to a distance of more than 300 meters. The recommended routes provided by Dijkstra's algorithm showed good agreement with Google Maps' recommendations. Another advantage of the Twinguard system is its portable and efficient design.

articleTitle: The Implementation of ISO 37301:2021 on Compliance Management System (CMS) to Improve Product Quality for Customer Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to guide the implementation of the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 37301:2021 on Compliance Management System (CMS) effectively through compliance contract management to improve the product quality of an Indonesian manufacture-company for achieving its consumer/customer's satisfaction. Compliance to contractual requirements to achieve customer satisfaction should not only rely per se on the contract requirements as stated in the contract, but also consider customer's concerns on product quality. It has become the finding of this academic research that by integrating the Kano Model into contractual compliance management in the Company, the Company's product quality improved and attracted its customer. Such improvement is resulted from the ability of the Company in its CMS strategy by interpreting the provisions of the contract within the perspective of Kano's satisfaction quadrants.

articleTitle: Designing Token-based Crowdfunding System on Private Blockchain Network for Indonesian Cooperative Investment Accountability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Crowdfunding, an increasingly popular form of community fundraising, allows individuals to contribute funds to support various projects collectively. This method's growth is attributed to the widespread use of social media and crowdfunding platforms. Despite its effectiveness in resource mobilization, crowdfunding faces challenges in ensuring se-cure funding handling and maintaining transparency and accountability. This study presents a novel approach tailored for Indonesian cooperatives, crucial in driving economic and community growth, proposing a token-based crowdfunding model using Hyperledger Fabric's private blockchain network. It ensures secure, immutable transaction records and incor-porates digital tokens representing equity, debt, or rewards. This approach addresses complex regulatory frameworks and emphasizes the need for stringent accountability and security measures while introducing asset representation and liquidity in fundraising. Implementing such a system promises to modernize cooperative fundraising, improving financial inclusivity and community engagement while adhering to local standards.

articleTitle: Estimating Anxiety Intensity of Dementia Patients Using Phrases, Facial Expressions, and Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Recently, the number of persons with dementia (PwD) has been steadily increasing. The PwDs live with anxiety derived from the decline in cognitive function, leading to concerns about memory loss and the future. The accumulation of these anxieties causes a state of agitation and Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD). Dealing with BPSD becomes a burden on the caregivers and the PwDs and violates their wellbeing. It is becoming a social issue. When a caregiver deals with agitation and BPSD, dealing with the early stages gives a smaller load than managing the escalated stage of agitation. Therefore, predicting agitation and BPSD in advance reduces the burden on caregivers and PwD and improves their wellbeing. Several methods have been proposed to predict BPSD using physiological, environmental, and caregiving data. However, there is a lack of research considering the state of feeling anxiety. Also, using a device that touches the skin tends to make PwD stressed, and continuous measurement is difficult. Thus, estimating anxiety from information obtained without contacting devices is necessary. Our research group has developed a metric, the CADATY index. The index is designed to estimate the intensity of anxiety and agitation based on the daily life situations of PwDs. We propose a method for estimating the CADATY index using Bayesian estimation by acquiring multimodal observation information such as phrases, facial expressions, and behaviors as the daily life of PwDs. To evaluate our method, we collect these data by recording video and audio in a nursing home that provides elderly housing with supportive services, i.e., in a daily living environment. We could estimate the CADATY index value in cases where we captured every modality. We found that the information from phrases and behaviors effectively detected signs of agitation and BPSD.

articleTitle: Interactive Learning Through Virtual Reality Operating Training Simulations for Industry Operators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In the manufacturing industry, factory operations encounter three primary conditions: normal, start-up, and shutdown, each necessitating specialized handling for efficiency and safety. Manual training to address these conditions often proves suboptimal, intricate, time-consuming, and poses high safety risks. To tackle this issue, this research proposes and develops a Virtual Reality (VR)-based Operator Training Simulator (OTS). The VR OTS enables interactive and realistic simulation training from the perspective of both field operators and control panel operators. he development process involved iterative design and testing phases, incorporating feedback from a sample of 50 operators to ensure usability and realism. Data analysis was performed to evaluate the simulator's impact on training efficiency and effectiveness. Research findings indicate that this VR application successfully generates highly realistic simulations for normal, start-up, and shutdown conditions, enhancing operator readiness and skills. Its performance is also adequate with a frame rate of 72 frames per second (FPS) and a manageable CPU and GPU load. Further studies are warranted to optimize OTS with other immersive technologies to bolster training efficiency.

articleTitle: Business Strategy Analysis of EPC to Improve Corporate Performance: Case on State-Owned Construction Company
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The EPC business in Indonesia has experienced rapid growth, with a projected annual increase of 5.5% from 2018 to 2022, propelled mainly by substantial investments in infrastructure. This sector plays a pivotal role in fostering economic growth. One state-owned construction company, established in 1953, has contributed significantly to infrastructure development but faces challenges such as revenue fluctuations and intense competition. From 2018 to 2022, the EPC sector's profitability declined due to internal inefficiencies and competition. This study bridges the gap between national EPC growth and the decline in company performance by employing a qualitative descriptive approach to investigate the underlying causes and propose strategic solutions. Data were gathered from questionnaires, interviews, company documents, and literature. The McKinsey framework, Internal Factor Evaluation (IFE), and External Factor Evaluation (EFE) analyses were used, along with the SWOT matrix and Quantitative Strategy Planning Matrix (QSPM). Seven key strategies were identified based on their Total Attractive Scores: developing human resources (7,002), establishing partnerships (6,993), enhancing technological capabilities (6,039), achieving cost efficiency (5,736), strengthening contractual capabilities (5,524), integrating technology into value engineering (5,407), and leveraging governmental relationships (4,822).

articleTitle: Forecasting Pipelines Operating Pressure: A Proactive Approach to Prevent Oil Congealing Using ARIMA, FFNN, and Hybrid Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Effective management of operational pressure in oil pipeline is crucial for ensuring flow assurance and preventing disruptions such as oil congealing. This study explores the efficacy of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Feedforward Neural Networks (FFNN), and a hybrid model combining both ARIMA and FFNN in forecasting operational pressure in a section of pipeline. Utilizing historical pressure data from an oil pipeline in Indonesia, the study compares these models based on their forecasting accuracy, evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The goal is to identify the most effective predictive model as a data- driven basis for Company in aiding preventive measures in pipeline operations. The study highlights how FFNN model outperformed other models, achieving an RMSE of 15.42 and a MAPE of 14.53. These result demonstrate the FFNN's potential to enhance operational pressure management, providing a reliable, data-driven basis for preventive measures in pipeline operations, thereby improving operational safety and reducing the risk of costly disruptions, indicating its potential utility in operational pressure management systems.

articleTitle: The Conceptual Framework of National and Global Values on Food Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Food security has been a maj or issue in most part of the world now and is expected to becoming more critical in the future. It is therefore each country put substantial effort in creating food security for their respective nation. With the abundant of natural resources in Indonesia it is important for all stakeholders to act in the most responsible and sustainable way. In the context of Indonesia, we believe that food security may have ties to the societies common ground or values. There are national and global values that need to be embraced more firmly by stakeholders in the food system to improve food security in Indonesia. To more effectively embrace those values, there is a need to design a training system for stakeholders in food systems that include government officials, maj or food producers and distributors, logistics players and the customers. The purpose of the paper is to propose a framework that links food security with some common ground in the societies such as social justice, sense of national unity and sustainability and how training systems can be established to support this linkage. The paper is based on a literature review. We aim to identify the factors related to national and global values and establish some propositions.

articleTitle: Film Industry Multi-Level Competitiveness: A Comparative Literature Review of Porter's Strategic Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Competitiveness has been a central focus for academics and practitioners in many different sectors since the 1980s. Many studies in the film sector have examined competitiveness, its implications, and applications. However, there is a lack of comprehensive reviews summarizing and critiquing existing research on the multi-level approach to competitiveness within the film industry. This literature review addresses this gap by evaluating competitiveness at national, industry, cluster, and firm levels through the lens of Porter's competitive framework, employing comparative analysis and hermeneutic content analysis. The study synthesizes recent findings on film industry competitiveness and identifies key areas for future research.

articleTitle: Sustainable Technology Innovations: Optimizing Inverter Selection for Solar PV and Wind Turbine Systems Using Fuzzy MCDM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Selecting the appropriate inverters is essential for optimizing the efficiency and performance of solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine systems, as these choices directly affect energy conversion and overall system output. Critical factors such as cost, compatibility with renewable energy sources, efficiency, reliability, and safety must be meticulously evaluated. Hence, a systematic and comprehensive approach is required for the assessment and comparison of various inverter options. This study utilizes Multi-Criteria Decision-Making with Fuzzy Logic Set (F-MCDM), incorporating the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to evaluate the identified criteria and employing the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (F-TOPSIS) with fuzzy logic to rank the options. The findings highlight smart grid inverters as the optimal solutions, effectively addressing issues of compatibility, reliability, efficiency, safety, and cost. The proposed methodology yields a significant total equity value of USD 9,325.71, with notable annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) amounting to USD 1,601.37. The estimated payback period is 7.59 years, with an impressive return on investment (ROI) of 229.29%. Additionally, the net income considerably lowered production costs, amounting to USD 30,708.6 in a single period.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Framework of Halal Traceability System in Indonesia Cosmetics Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Halal regulation in Indonesia has been extended to include food and products related to the body, such as cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and personal care items, ensuring that they adhere to halal standards. Although obtaining a halal certificate is essential, many industries face significant challenges in fully implementing this regulation despite their efforts. Ensuring halal integrity requires robust traceability. Our study uses a semi-systematic literature review to identify key themes and gaps in the research related to the topic in a top-level field. This study proposes a research framework to identify the antecedents of halal implementation. The proposed framework draws on institutional theory and resource-based views. The primary proposition is that a combination of external pressure and organizational capability is crucial in implementing a halal traceability system.

articleTitle: Nickel Price Prediction Using Bi-Directional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) and Attention Bi-Directional LSTM Network (At-Bi-LSTM)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The fluctuatives trend of nickel price possess significant challenges to nickel mining and smelting company, that possess high financial risk due to its capital intensiveness trait. Providing decision maker with robust price prediction model, can help the business leader to create more relevant and reasonable business decision, either in daily operations or long term investment. Such method to aid price prediction has been employed, one of which is using deep learning method such as Long Short Term Memory (LSTM). This model, promise better predictive capability compared to more traditional model, due to its capability in capturing more complex pattern in the data. However, in more chaotic time - series trend, this model also prone to inaccuracy, due to difficulties to capture more random fluctuation. This research aims to investigate price prediction model using bi-directional LSTM, further enhanced with attention mechanism, which recently gained more attention per se because it allows the model to focus on specific trends in the data, that helps explained short term and long-term fluctuation of the model. The results of this research, show that Bi-LSTM model can outperform LSTM model obtained from other research, while attention Bi-LSTM still outperformed by both Bi-LSTM and the previous model. Further research is needed to confirm the methods capability in dealing with more complex and fluctuative time series trend.

articleTitle: Navigating Consumer Skepticism: Conceptual Model of Distrust Detection and Recognition Technology Adoption Among Online Shop Owners in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Background: Consumer skepticism affects trust between online shoppers and shop owners in digital commerce, necessitating effective distrust detection mechanisms. This study presents a conceptual model aimed at promoting the adoption of distrust detection and recognition technology among online shop owners, focusing on technologies powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). The model builds on Taylor's Decomposed Theory of Planned Behavior (DTPB) and incorporates factors relevant to online shop owners' perceptions of consumer distrust. Method: A quantitative research approach was used to survey 100 online shop owners to validate the model empirically. Results: The results indicate a significant effect of Perceived Usefulness (PU) and Social Influence (SI) on intention to adopt the technology. For small businesses such as online shops, PU (an internal factor) and SI (an external factor) can predict owners' intention to adopt distrust detection technology. Implications: This study highlights a simplified method for measuring small business owners' intention to adopt advanced information technologies and suggests business opportunities for e-commerce platforms to strategically position online shop owners.

articleTitle: Productivity Improvement Through Energy Efficiency Training in Manufacturing Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This study examines the impact of integrating energy efficiency training with energy audits in Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) programs on employee behavior, productivity, and energy consumption in the automotive manufacturing sector. Using a quantitative approach with a descriptive analytical method, the research involved 100 randomly selected employees. Data were collected through energy audits, surveys, and interviews. Descriptive statistical analyses were used to evaluate changes in energy awareness and productivity. The findings demonstrate that integrating energy efficiency training with energy audits significantly increases employee awareness and productivity while reducing energy consumption. This approach provides long-term benefits for operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, offering robust empirical support for energy management practices. The results indicate that energy audits not only serve as evaluation tools but also enhance employees' energy awareness and promote sustainable behavioral changes. Despite limitations, such as the focus on the automotive sector and potential respondent bias, the study highlights the practicality of integrating energy audits into training programs. This research enriches the existing literature by demonstrating that the synergy between training and auditing leads to more effective energy management. The findings advocate for broader adoption of integrated approaches in manufacturing to improve operational efficiency and achieve sustainability goals.

articleTitle: The Impact of RBV on the Sustainability of FnB SMEs in Malang: The Roles of SCMP and Tax Compliance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Relevance: The sustainability of Food and Beverage (FnB) Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Malang City is crucial for economic growth and job creation, given their dominant role in the local business landscape. However, challenges like resource constraints and operational issues threaten their sustainability, necessitating comprehensive research and strategic interventions. Research objective: This study evaluates and enhances the sustainability of FnB MSMEs in Malang City using the Resource-Based View (RBV) theory. It focuses on key variables-Ambidexterity, Socioemotional Wealth (SEW), and Entrepreneurship Orientation (EO)-while exploring SCMP's mediating role and Tax Compliance's moderating effect. Data and methods: Using an explanatory quantitative approach and SmartPLS 4 for analysis tool. A robust sample of 380 FnB MSMEs in Malang City contributes to the study's reliability and validity. These methods provide insights into variable impacts on sustainability. Results: Preliminary findings show SEW and EO significantly impacting FnB MSME sustainability, with SCMP mediating Ambidexterity and SEW. Tax Compliance moderates EO's effect, underlining its role in long-term sustainability planning. Conclusions: This study's findings offer actionable strategies for households, policymakers, and business owners to enhance FnB MSME resilience and performance. By analyzing key variables and their relationships, the research contributes to developing policies supporting sustainability and growth in Malang City's FnB MSME sector.

articleTitle: Building Composite Performance Index for Broadband Internet Customer Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The global trend in broadband internet services reveals an increased focus on reliability, customer service, and integrating new technologies like IoT, 5G, or FMC. Customer service is primarily determined by network quality and reliability, price, and the quality of customer support provided by ISPs. Meanwhile, existing network quality measurement methods often involve numerous parameters, ranging from download speed and server response time to video streaming quality, each providing a separate insight into aspects of user experience. Therefore, the importance of the composite index method is becoming increasingly relevant. This method allows the integration of these various parameters into a single, easily understandable integrated index, simplifying complex data analysis into a more concise and interpretable form. As a result of this approach, internet service providers can more effectively monitor and enhance the customer experience and the overall quality of their services for various purposes with a single composite parameter value, providing reassurance and confidence in their operations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Human Activity Recognition Framework for Wearable Devices Based on Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has been a highly debated topic in recent years. Due to privacy concerns, especially in smart home environments, sensor-based HAR is commonly employed. This method involves users carrying smart devices, such as smartwatches or smartphones, that calculate tri-axial acceleration through gyroscopes to determine specific activities. However,Many users and developers do not fully comprehend deep learning and other algorithms. Users often worry about the unknown, and the development of HAR based on wearable devices will become increasingly challenging for developers. Consequently, the concept of Explainable AI (XAI) has been introduced to allow human users to understand and trust the machine learning algorithms and the results they produce. In this paper, we used the UCI dataset to analyze the factors that significantly influence the machine learning model with a CNN-LSTM architecture, employing XAI techniques to provide a clear demonstration of these impacts.

articleTitle: Exploring AI Applications in Digital Art Creation of Hanoman Balinese Dance Animation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This paper examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the digital creation of Balinese dance animations, with a specific focus on the Hanoman dance character as the case study. Hanoman dance as a part of Balinese dance, known for its intricate movements, unique costume and cultural significance, presents a unique challenge for digital artists. AI technologies, such as machine learning and computer vision, offer novel approaches to capturing and animating these complex dance forms. This study examines current AI applications in this domain, assesses their effectiveness, and discusses the potential advancements and limitations. Through the use of rotoscoping and motion capture techniques, this study adeptly examines the intricate movements of the Hanoman dance, an integral part of Balinese dance heritage, employing text-to-animation and AI models for video footage motion capture. The thorough processes of data collection, preprocessing, and model training emphasized in the study highlight the necessity of a meticulous methodology. Furthermore, incorporating expert feedback during the validation and refinement phases ensures that the digital representations are both authentic and expressive. The study concludes that AI technologies can play a crucial role in preserving Balinese dance, offering educational tools and digital archives that uphold the cultural integrity of this traditional art form.

articleTitle: Forecasting Quezon City's Rooftop Solar Energy Potential Using Ensemble Regression with AdaBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The continuing rise in electricity consumption in the Philippines combined with the global issue of climate change calls for the need of a more sustainable source of electricity. Solar energy is ideally suited for the Philippines as it is near the equator. Urban cities can also take advantage of integrating solar panels in their infrastructure to produce energy. This study aims to forecast the rooftop solar energy potential of Quezon City by utilizing geographic information system (GIS) and Ensemble Regression with Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost). Three regression models were designed to forecast solar irradiance. Decision Tree Regression, Ensemble Regression with Gradient Boosting, and Ensemble Regression with Adaptive Boosting models were compared using their Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Average Error (MAE), and Correlation of Determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) values. The Ensemble Regression with Adaptive Boosting model outperformed the other models during training validation while also being more robust against overfitting during testing validation. Combining the rooftop polygons gathered from GIS software with the Ensemble Regression with AdaBoost, the solar rooftop potential of Quezon City was projected to be 30,745,119 kWh per month.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation Printing Service Using Design Thinking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Lafamilia Printing is a prominent offset-printing company situated in Bogor that operates on a conventional business model that has not yet been integrated with customer service and administrative management. This lack of integration poses challenges in targeting customers, and it is imperative that the printing shop digitize its business processes to facilitate target customers, enhance internal management, and streamline customer ordering, payment, and production process tracking. By digitizing its operations, Lafamilia Printing can also extend its reach to a wider consumer base. We use the design thinking method, which involves a comprehensive analysis of user needs to identify solutions to complex problems. The findings of this study indicate that both customers and employees require digital transformation, with features tailored to their individual needs. New customers require online ordering features, order tracking, online reviews, and online payments, whereas existing customers still need online order tracking features, product information, discount prices, and quick access to customer service. Employees require administrative transformations, such as customer and order recaps and online invoices. The number of consumer orders has a direct impact on employee salaries; therefore, it is crucial to consider the needs of both groups. In this study, we identified differences in the needs of new and regular customers and found that no printing application currently integrates the number of products ordered with employee salaries.

articleTitle: Wood Species Classification Based on Wood Porosity Distribution of Macroscopic Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In the context of illegal logging, it is crucial to identify the wood species that are being traded. Wood species classification plays a vital role in inspecting the movement of wood in and out of an area. Furthermore, wood classification is particularly significant to determine the species of the wood test sample to obtain high accuracy. Therefore, the development of automatic wood species classification based on computer vision is highly required. Each wood species possesses unique anatomical characteristics, such as its vessel or pore structure. This research aims to propose an automatic algorithm that can classify wood species based on the porosity distribution of the macroscopic image. This research utilized wood images from six different wood species. The Contour method is used to identify pores first and then many features will be extracted. It will detect the pore size and extract pore features such as the number of pores, size, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, and density. By using the macroscopic image of the six wood species, the result showed that 300 data could be extracted and forming a model based on pore features. The accuracy of the wood classification was evaluated using the Random Forest classifier, yielding an accuracy rate of 92.00%. This indicates that the wood porosity distribution features can be effectively utilized for wood species classification.

articleTitle: Wind Energy Potential of High-Rise Buildings in Makati Using Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Ayala Avenue is considered the heart of Makati's central business district due to several major banks, corporations, embassies, and business establishments. Despite its financial and economic significance, it experienced notable power interruptions in the past which led to significant risks and losses. To provide an alternative power source, the study aims to evaluate the wind energy potential in the area due to the wind tunneling effect of high-rise buildings. A digital twin of Ayala Avenue was created through RWind Simulation where the area's meteorological data and the buildings’ dimensions were reflected to be simulated and analyzed. The results show a significant increase in wind speed and wind power with values ranging from 11.5 – 13.5 m/s and 850 to 1140 watts respectively. This indicates that the high-rise buildings in Ayala Avenue, Makati City are viable for wind power generation which can be used as a backup power source for low-power utility equipment to be used along Ayala Avenue.

articleTitle: Strategic Management for Enhancing Water Quality in the Barito River Basin Through Cost Optimization Using Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The Barito River Basin, a crucial water resource in Indonesia, is facing significant environmental challenges due to rapid urbanization, industrialization, and agricultural activities. These activities have led to the degradation of water quality, posing threats to both the ecosystem and the communities reliant on the river. This study proposes a strategic management framework aimed at enhancing water quality in the Barito River Basin through cost optimization using Linear Programming (LP). By integrating LP techniques, the study seeks to identify the most cost-effective measures for pollution control and resource allocation, ensuring compliance with water quality standards. The approach involves formulating an objective function to minimize the total cost of implementing water treatment and pollution mitigation strategies while satisfying constraints related to pollutant levels such as pH, Total Suspended Solids (TSS), Iron (Fe), Manganese (Mn), Dissolved Oxygen (DO), and Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD). The study demonstrates the application of LP in selecting optimal combinations of treatment methods, such as the use of Lime and Caustic Soda, to achieve the desired water quality at minimal costs. The results underscore the potential of LP in facilitating sustainable water management practices, balancing economic and environmental objectives, and supporting decision-makers in developing effective policies for the preservation of the Barito River Basin.

articleTitle: Organizational Transformation for Business Sustainability and Growth in Public Service Corporations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Public service companies are essential in society, providing reliable, affordable, high-quality services focused on customer satisfaction while meeting stakeholder expectations and regulations for sustainable business growth. Strategy innovation is necessary to achieve these goals. In Indonesia, public service companies are particularly consolidated by state-owned enterprises (SOEs), which the government fully owns. SOEs innovate by forming holding companies, which the government sees as the most effective way to create synergy. Studies show that 60%-70% of organizational changes fail, highlighting the importance of successful transformation in public companies. Ensuring smooth transitions with minimal disruption while maintaining service quality is crucial for good organizational performance in public service corporations. Efficiency in transformations and transitions can be achieved through change management. This study evaluates various change management factors and frameworks, examining their impact on organizational performance using the 7s McKinsey Change Model. The research involves a literature review, surveys, and descriptive statistical analysis. The results indicate that change management factors in the McKinsey model influence organizational performance. However, the optimal change management model for public companies remains undetermined, presenting opportunities for further research.

articleTitle: Candidate Selection of Water Shut-Off in Oil and Gas Industry Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The water production is a major issue faced by most of oil and gas companies. The increase of water production leads to an increase of maintenance cost, failure in fulfilling energy (oil and gas) needs, and loss of profit due to decline of oil and gas production. To address the escalating water production issue, most of the companies, one of which is PT Indo Migas, employ water shut-off (WSO) activities aiming for mitigating water production, thus maximizing oil and gas recovery from reservoirs. Despite these efforts, the success rate of WSO activities at PT Indo Migas remains low as historical WSO results are not taking into account in candidate selection, leading to financial losses and operational complexities. To overcome this challenge, this study introduces a predictive model based on the random forest algorithm to improve WSO candidate selection. The model utilizes historical operational data and relevant reservoir, production, and geological data to analyze and classify potential WSO candidate. Key findings indicate that variables such as water production, well depth, and reservoir pressure significantly influence the WSO candidate selection process. Through data analysis and model development, the predictive model identifies 12 out of 65 wells as suitable candidates for WSO activities. The model achieves an accuracy rate of 83 % and sensitivity of 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> despite of little amount of trained data. The implementation of the developed model's recommendations can give significant managerial implications for PT Indo Migas and similar companies in the oil and gas sector.

articleTitle: Autonomous Drive-Through System Using EasyOCR and Dobot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative approach to revolutionize drive-through operations in the retail sector through autonomous technologies, focusing on the critical role of optical character recognition (OCR) for recognizing Thai license plates. The integration of DoBot technology with OCR addresses common issues such as order accuracy, wait times, and operational inefficiencies inherent in traditional drive-through models. Our license plate detection model exhibits impressive performance, achieving an accuracy of 97.47%, precision of 98.10%, recall of 99.35%, and an F1 score of 98.73%, underscoring its ability to accurately identify license plates with minimal false positives. However, the OCR system's character recognition rate of 74.04<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> indicates moderate accuracy, suggesting areas for enhancement. This system enables precise vehicle identification, personalized order processing, and secure payment, streamlining the entire ordering process. By leveraging DoBot technology for autonomous order delivery, we enhance overall operational efficiency and reduce the workload and number of workers required, thereby lowering labor costs and improving productivity. Future efforts will focus on improving OCR preprocessing techniques and algorithms to better handle challenging Thai characters, further enhancing the system's reliability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Risk Management Practices using the House of Risk for Safety, Health, etc.(HORshe) Method: A Case Study on Wastewater Treatment in the Pharmaceutical Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The pharmaceutical industry in Indonesia is expanding rapidly despite environmental challenges. PT. XYZ, a major player, faces significant difficulties in managing liquid waste. The current Liquid Waste Disposal Permit (IPLC) is deficient, inadequately addressing domestic wastewater quality standards and broader environmental sustainability measures. A comprehensive legislative framework covering all technical and environmental aspects, including household wastewater, is necessary. This study introduces the House of Risk for Safety, Health, etc. (HORshe) approach, an advanced model integrating methodologies from HOR (House of Risk), HoQ (House of Quality), FMEA (Failure Mode and Effect Analysis), and HIRA (Hazard Identification and Risk Analysis). HORshe expands risk management to include safety, health, and environmental considerations, emphasizing preventive measures to mitigate risk agents. The research utilizes the HORshe model to identify effective wastewater control strategies through qualitative interviews and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs). The study's significance lies in its application to pharmaceutical industrial waste management, addressing critical environmental risks and consumer safety concerns. The objective is to refine risk analysis across multiple sectors using the HORshe model and contribute to future research. The results suggest 11 preventive measures for 6 key risk factors out of a total of 12, with ultrafiltration identified as the most crucial preventive strategy, while reverse-osmosis control systems are deemed less significant. This highlights the research's impact on sustainable waste disposal practices in the pharmaceutical industry and other domains, providing a foundation for future improvements in environmental risk management.

articleTitle: Secure and Scalable LLM-Based Recommendation Systems: An MLOps and Security by Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into e-commerce recommendation systems promises to transform consumer interactions with products, enhancing discovery and engagement through personalized recommendations. This approach has become vital for improving user experience and boosting sales. However, the adoption of LLMs introduces significant security and scalability challenges. To address these issues, this paper proposes an innovative framework that combines machine learning operations (MLOps) with security-by-design principles, with the aim of creating LLM -based recommendation systems that are secure and scalable for e-commerce platforms. This study explores the entire life cycle of an LLM-based recommendation system, from data preprocessing and model training to deployment and continuous monitoring, while embedding security and scalability. By implementing Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) with security-by-design principles, e-commerce businesses can leverage the advanced capabilities of LLMs to provide personalized shopping experiences, increase user engagement, and drive sales without compromising user trust and system performance.

articleTitle: Purchasing Intention of Tour Package Brands in Access to Digital Technology and User Generated Content on Bali Travel Tour
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Digital technology is currently a vital medium to influence consumers with diverse behaviours and a high level of sensitivity when purchasing goods and services. The purpose of this study is to analyse the impact of exposure to digital technology and user-generated content on the brand purchase intention of travel packages in the Bali tourism sector. As digital technology changes the way we communicate or convey information to attract consumers, one of the methods used to attract consumers is user-generated content (UGC) to create a more intimate engagement between products, services, and consumers. A total of 200 tourists who bought tour packages were used as respondents using accidental sampling. The results of the study explain that digital technology and user integration center have a significant influence on brand purchase intention, and brand exposure and brand familiarity have a considerable positive influence on brand purchase intention. A different influence is found: brand knowledge and attitude have a negative impact on brand purchase intention. The results of this study can enrich knowledge about the currently developing topic of e-marketing aimed at academics. From a practical perspective, this research can provide marketers with insight into the effectiveness of content as an advertising platform in the travel and tourism industry.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review on Blockchain-based Cybersecurity Models for Ransomware Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) examines blockchain-based cybersecurity models designed for ransomware mitigation, addressing the significant threat ransomware poses to organizations globally. By systematically identifying, evaluating, and synthesizing studies from academic journals and conferences, the review highlights blockchain's effectiveness in ensuring data integrity, enhancing transparency, and strengthening cybersecurity frameworks. Various applications of blockchain in ransomware mitigation are discussed, showcasing its ability to disrupt traditional attack vectors. The review also compares key models, assesses their strengths and limitations, and identifies critical challenges and future research directions. This SLR provides valuable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers, underscoring the transformative potential of blockchain technology in combating ransomware and advancing a secure digital ecosystem.

articleTitle: Mobile Crowd Sensing with Secure Coin Rewarding in Human Activity Recognition for Elderly People System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Mobile Crowd Sensing (MCS) is a promising approach that harnesses the collective intelligence of mobile devices to gather data, particularly beneficial for monitoring the daily activities of elderly individuals. This paper proposes a system that integrates secure coin rewarding with MCS for Human Activity Recognition in elderly care. By addressing challenges such as data security, privacy attacks, and incentivizing healthy behaviors, the system aims to enhance the well-being of elderly individuals. Pairing-based cryptography is employed to ensure privacy preservation, while a reward system motivates active participation and data accuracy. The proposed system operates through a series of steps involving key generation, challenge authentication, receipt issuance, and reward claiming. Latency measurements demonstrate the efficiency of the system in issuing receipts and claiming rewards. Overall, this research contributes to the advancement of monitoring systems for elderly care by combining technology, community engagement, and personalized recommendations to promote healthy living among the elderly population.

articleTitle: Validation of an Academic Resilience Scale for Indonesian University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: Higher education fostered university students' academic competence and professional development, especially post-pandemic. Academic resilience, crucial for student success, lacked a validated Indonesian tool. Validating the ARS-30 Scale was essential to evaluate students' risk assessment and adaptation to academic challenges. The study, involving 500 university students from various cities, aimed to validate the academic resilience scale in the Indonesian context. Data collection included translation, validity, and reliability assessments. The Content Validity Index (CVI) values ranged from. 87 to 1. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) showed an acceptable fit with Chi-Square=289.629, RMSEA=.053, CFI=.945. And factor loadings from. 50 to. 73. The Cronbach alpha was. 735. Fourteen items showed a good fit, and sixteen items showed a poor fit. The study concluded that the scale effectively measures academic resilience in Indonesian university students.

articleTitle: Early Warning Forecasting of Large Induction Motor in the Oil and Gas Industry from Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: In the oil and gas industry, the reliability and performance of induction motors are critical for operations such as pumps, compressors, and drilling equipment. Traditional condition monitoring techniques like vibration analysis and thermography often fall short in providing early warning signals and accurate predictions. This study investigates the application of machine learning, particularly deep learning, to enhance fault diagnosis and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of large induction motors. By utilizing winding temperature data, the research develops and evaluates hybrid deep learning models that integrate Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, alongside a Transformer model. The Transformer model demonstrates superior performance in prediction accuracy compared to the hybrid CNN-LSTM model. The proposed models show significant improvements in early fault detection and RUL prediction, offering potential benefits in maintenance strategies, cost savings, and system reliability. The study highlights that incorporating additional parameters such as power consumption, bearing vibration, and ambient temperature could further enhance the robustness of the models. Future research should focus on addressing data quality, model generalization, and real-time application challenges to optimize maintenance schedules and extend motor lifespan in the oil and gas industry.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Neural Networks for Electrical Load Forecasting in Renewable Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
abstract: The problem of electrical load forecasting represents a crucial aspect in many Smart Grid applications. In Renewable Energy Communities, an effective Energy Management System, aiming at improving clean energy consumption and energy self-sufficiency, schedules the operations of the available controllable loads and energy storage systems necessarily relying on load forecasts. Obtaining accurate load predictions is a particularly challenging task, given the randomness inherent in the electrical load time series. As such, advanced Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning techniques may result ineffective if additional information (e.g., external temperature) is not provided. Since these data are often not accessible, this paper studies the performance of low-complexity models, based on Feed-Forward Neural Networks, applied to the forecasting of the mere electrical load signal. This kind of approach in the context of an Energy Management System presents two major advantages: first, fast-trainable neural models can be retrained online to adapt to new consumption habits, without affecting the operations of the Energy Management System; second, a short inference time allows for having more time for other demanding operations, namely the communication with metering and actuating devices and the elaboration of the control strategy. The results on an open-source electrical load database show that the proposed models can achieve a forecasting accuracy comparable to recurrent networks, but with shorter training and inference time.

articleTitle: Developing Maturity Matrix: Measuring Banking Sector Readiness in Digital Corporate Governance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Consumer Technology (ISCT)
